This. This mod right here. This one. Download it. Use it. Love it. Thank the creator and give him a big hug for it.
Also, some advice for people who are getting frustrated with the steep difficulty curve.
1. Always bring a rookie and upgrade the squad size ASAP. The more competent soldiers you have the less you have to worry about them taking a plasma round to the kneecaps. I have a good baker's dozen of guys who are at LEAST sargeants.
2. Sharpshooters. Get a couple and make SURE they have the Long Watch ability. Having a sniper or two providing cover fire for your squad can save your damn life.
3. Stop, wait, reload. If your mission doesn't have a 'finish in X turns or you're screwed' timer, don't be afraid to pause, reload your weapons, and have a few guys go into overwatch... ESPECIALLY when reinforcements are coming. There are few things greater than seeing a freshly deployed squad of Advent soldiers get torn apart by a hail of gunfire before they can get a single shot off becuase your entire squad was in overwatch waiting for them.
4. When all else fails, use fire. Grenades, rockets, etc. Don't be afraid to blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up. You might lose some stuff, but it's worth it if you can make your life easier in the long run. Blow up cover so that your other units can get a clear shot, blast an enemy to knock them out of overwatch or suppressing fire, etc. This is ESPECIALLY useful when cars, tanker trucks, or other flammable things are involved as they'll explode too and deal bonus damage. I've seen squads of sectoids and vipers rain down gently across the landscape from one well placed explosive.
5. To hell with the civvies, focus on the X-rays. Y'know those rescue missions where you can evac civilians? Civvies are♥♥♥♥♥♥at staying in cover. The best way to protect them is to kill the aliens before they can kill them. Let them run around in a panic and give ET something else to worry about, namely your friend Mr. Boomstick.
6. Sectoids die FAST AND HARD. They can mind control your guys, they can make them panic or disorient them, they can even play necromancer and bring their guys back from the dead as zombies. Kill the ♥♥♥♥ers first! Also, when they die those effects go poof with them. Very useful~
7. R&D and Communications are vital. Whenever you make contact with a new region the first thing you should always do is build a comm tower, the more you have the more supply the resistance sends you each month. Also, if you have a chance to recruit an engineer, ALWAYS take it! Engineers are key to managing your ship. The more you have the more power you'll have, the more regions you can contact, your research will go faster in the Proving Grounds, and so on. Your squad can be skilled enough to bring a tear to G.I. Joe's eye, but if they're using rubber band guns and wearing football padding for armor it won't matter.
8. Don't be afraid to restart. XCOM 2 is almost a roguelike in some respects. Don't be afraid to stop and retry with the knowledge you've gained from this playthrough. Sometimes you're backed into a corner and simply can't win. It happens.
9. The Steam Workshop is your friend. Besides the Quiet Bradford! mod (and again, big thanks to the mod's creator) there's a whole host of other useful ones I've found. Some will give rookies a small boost to aim to help even out the difficulty, some will slow or even stop the Avatar Project timer. This game is a really nasty one sometimes and there's no shame in adding a couple mods to help if its just too difficult to enjoy.

As of this writing I have only played the base Fallout 4 game and haven't delved into the DLC, nor have I explored mods. I picked up Fallout 4 for $20 during a Steam sale, and it was well worth the money. Although the game is buggy as is typical for Bethesda's Fallout and Elder Scrolls games, it represents a beautiful update to the Fallout series. I fell in love immediately with the settlement building system, and am in the middle of my second playthrough of the game. I always play as sniper ninja, and in my current playthrough have passed through the barrier where combat is a struggle at younger levels but peaks and becomes too easy once you level up and mod out the right legendary guns. This is not a complaint, but I suppose I could use a mod that fiddles with the balance.
My biggest complaint concerning the base game are the endings, and there will be spoilers coming up. A feature of Fallout 4 is the ability to have a companion travel with the player, and as you level up their affinity for you they reveal portions of their story. Although NPCs are very difficult to play with as the sniper ninja and in a practical sense I hate all of them with fiery burning passion, I do like their stories, and I even get a little attached to them. If you have taken the time to befriend the various companion characters in the game then you should know that there is no ending in which you do not end up killing some of them, and that is to say nothing about the other NPCs in each faction who you are also required to kill to progress. To make matters worse, the reasons given fall somewhere between hamfisted and fanatical. It made for a sorely disappointing storytelling experience.
Overall, I would still recommend this game. I suspect many of you will not have the problem with the narrative that I did, and outside of this it was a beautiful, engrossing, and satisfying game, and well worth the price of admission.

I've been slowly crawling my way through this game and enjoying it a ton.  It's challenging and engaging with an aesthetic you can practically taste.  I've lost countless heroes and been tragically unlucky at the most important of moments.  It is only now, on Week 115 of my Campaign, that I finally say, "♥♥♥♥ this game in it's gaping RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."
On my way to defeat the last Boss on my list before delving into the Darkest Dungeon itself, I chose a group of hardy warriors, having proven themselves more than capable countless times.  I knew full well it was more than likely that they would not return.
However, their trek through the ruins seemed to be going remarkably well, and having cleared the last room before the Boss in question, they were all at full health and less than 10 stress.  I rested, buffed my team as best I could, and sent them off down the hallway towards their foe and, mayhaps, victory.
What they met was calamity and disaster.
The very first step into the halls saw them set upon by a common array of rabble, except for one little addition; a Doomsayer.  Hoping to kill him quickly, as they all to easily overwhelm the weak with their cursed words, I let loose the Houndmaster, Arbalest, and Hellion.  On the fifth turn, they were finally able to land a single blow.  He dodged 12 attacks in a row.  That single blow thankfully killed him, but the party was now in rough shape, and two of them dangerously close to having their resolve tested.  I bought some time to patch everyone up, and they moved ever forward once again...
Into an unburnt torch, and them into a Collector.
Who seemed intent on constantly summoning two Man-At-Arms to keep him Guarded.
But they won, and an array of crits kept my party whole but at half health across the board.  My Hellion needed only the smallest nudge to possibly lose herself, and the Vestal close behind.  The next step down the hall was blessedly empty, and I made the call to use the rest of my food to patch up the weakest of the party.
This proved to be folly, as their hunger decided to strike in the few moments before their final encounter.  They took 20% health damage, and my Hellion failed her resolve and turned to be Selfish.
Yet somehow, through Marks and luck, I was able to savagly set upon the Gibbering Prophet, reducing him to 52hp very quickly, and it seemed as though victory would be achieved despite the pitfalls.
I was sorely mistaken.
The Houndmaster hit him for 24, but resisted the Bleed.  The Hellion had done as she was instructed this entire time, but failed to cooperate in the last two turns before her demise to a tick of Blight on Deathsdoor, which was fair.  Arbalest hits for 18, Vestal is constantly spamming the area heal to keep everyone from deaths door, and I've finally run out of the stack of cures for Blight I brought with me.  The Prophet sets up the attack that will drop both the Houndmaster and Hellion to nill.
Hellion dies, Hound hits for 7 (somehow), Prophet resists the bleed, kills the Houndmaster, and leaves the Vestal and Arbalest right up front and my only prayer of doing those last 3HP of damage being Blind Fire and moving the Vestal to take the hits from above to buy him more time.
Now earlier, having my progress going to well, I took out one of the Wooden Pews for the extra gold because I'm always hurting for it pretty bad, and I counter myself lucky that I had one less target for it to randomly choose.
I somehow lasted another four turns and not once did he strike the Boss.
Now all of these things are to be expected in this game, and it is as harsh and unforgiving as it claims to be, but it is no longer worth my time to trudge through it.  I have failed my resolve test, and so ♥♥♥♥ this game.

"Such a dank and dismal place these warrens be," spoke Arthus the Crusader, "Yet we delve here to purge it of these abominations."
The path ahead was not only dank and dismal, but a path walked only by those who seek death. For the monsters within the warrens were not meant for the mortal realm.
Darkest Dungeons is a rogue-like dungeon explorer. The map is always changing as you explore several different areas from the Warrens to the Wealds. Your party of adventures, currently 28 in all, depart in groups of 4 into these devious places. Lepers, Crusaders, Vestals, and more join your party at the hamlet, the last sanction of humanity in the estate of your grandfather.

And while you can stock your parties with torches, food, and other items; none of these can prepare the adventurers like experience. For each successful journey will reward your parties with resolve, providing benefits and afflictions with each level. Disease, phobias, and more can infect your adventurers, but can be removed for a cost.
Darkest Dungeon is an excellent game. It makes you think. It makes you take risk. Each delve into the dungeons comes with a chance of glorious rewards. The atmosphere of the game really sells it, making each delve a dark journey into the unknown. Between the traps, monsters, and other events, Darkest Dungeon really gives some interesting challenges. With the more recent updates adding new classes, fixing mechanics, and removing bugs; it's really come together as a great game.
I highly recommend Darkest Dungeon if you want a challenging game with an eldritch horror vibe to it.

It's brilliant. You know how your first x-com ironman game ended in absolute failure? Well, that's canon.
Pros
- Complete modability.
- You are now the attacker. Nothing more X-Com-y than setting up a proper ambush and missing all your shots.
- Sectoids are now swole. They are proper aliens.
- The concealment system is pretty cool, plus we can now see who is in our FOV.
- I enjoy the timer based missions. There's a sense of urgency. I know a lot of people dislike them, but remember, we are the attackers. It would make no sense if the Advent did nothing to make sure how attacks fail.
Cons

- I would love more customization options for the soldiers. Perhaps most of them are just locked behind higher levels.
Seriously, if you loved the original (remake) X-Com, then buy this game. If you didn't like the original X-com, ask yourself why, and read if X-Com 2 has fixed what your originally hated.

XCOM 2 is a turn-based strategy developed by Firaxis and published by 2K Games. It is a direct sequel to the previous XCOM: Enemy Unknown and the expansion XCOM: Enemy Within.
In XCOM 2, follows the story where the XCOM lose the war to the alien. The aliens rule Earth, building shining cities that promise a brilliant future for humanity on the surface, while concealing a sinister agenda and eliminating all who dissent from their new order. So they said it, we are now on the offensive on XCOM 2. With only limited resources, XCOM must retake back Earth from the ADVENT.
XCOM 2 gameplay are quite similiar with XCOM: Enemy Unknown, but plays differently. In fact, you feel like you already knew how it plays out until you see the timer. Yes, each mission has a time limit to reach certain objectives. But most people describe it wrong as a turn timer or whatever it is they said. The truth is, it's a turn limit to reach certain objectives such as hacking a device, rescuing VIP or destroying key objectives. Most of them if completed, then the timer is gone and you can have all the time you want to kill the enemy. NOT all missions has this turn limit objectives however. Overwatch in XCOM 2 is even more powerful I think, even if some people didn't like the turn limit, overwatch now doesn't trigger all at once, they trigger one by one that you can be sure every overwatch is count. Base building retains the same element but building adjacent bonuses are gone, instead you get to upgrades with resources. The global map have been changed too. Since you have a mobile headquarters, in the global map, you need to move from place to place to scan for resources, intel or even contacting resistance on other location.
There is this thing called Avatar Project or simply AP by the community, I think, it renders your campaign has time limit which you have to act fast to delay or setback the project progress. You can do this by assaulting alien bases or hacking then kill the alien codex. There's also Dark Event, which some kind of random even that if left unchecked will, I say again WILL give you disadvantage and give the alien an advantage. Like XCOM: Enemy Unknown abduction mission, not all Dark Event mission can't be completed, you have to choose which you think is the best... or the worse. All of this makes your campaign has faster pace then the previous.
Tactical combat also has become more difficult, at least for me. I can see more challenge here. Remember Sectoid? They're not what you remember now, they posses more power and can mess you up if you don't kill them real quick. What about Thin Man? Now you will see the true form of the alien infiltration unit. Soldiers now also has even more useful abilities, some are in fact powerful if you know how to use them. Soldiers can even be upgraded further to gain more advantage, whether it's a weapon or the soldier themselves. Turn limit may be frustrating, but in my opinion they're not as frustrating as some people said.
Customization in XCOM 2 are great, I will say huge if they actually add more content or option into it, nevertheless we have modding support. There is a dedicated place where you can create you characters before you even play the campaign. Characters you created can be set to appear as XCOM soldiers, or VIP which is scientist or engineer, or even Dark VIP which will appear on some mission and you must capture them. With mods, customization will be unlimited.
Firaxis did improve the graphics and effects on XCOM 2. They look prettier than XCOM: Enemy Unknown. The downside XCOM 2 has is the performance. It is unoptimized that I can barely have FPS above 35. Most of the time I get stutters and lags. Mission loading time is quite long. They need to fix this.
Overall, XCOM 2 is a great sequel. Some people don't like the turn limit, but for me, knowing that we are on the offensive with guerilla style warfare, that's just about fair and challenging. With mods support is even better. If only the performance were better on release, I would give XCOM 2 way better score. I recommend XCOM 2.

Well, so far so good. Its essentially X-Com Enemy Unknown twenty years on with some upgrades so if you liked the first you'll enjoy this. Thats the good news.
The bad news is that this is a bigger 'bug' hunt than the Alien movies. Long load times, slowdown, problems recognizing when a turn is over, and so on make this game rather frustrating. Also, if Central doesn't shut up when a civilian gets shot in one of the retaliation missions I swear I'm going to hit him.
There definitely need to be some patches in this game's future, but once the issues are fixed (and Central is issued a ballgag) I'll definitely rank this game among one of my favorites.
UPDATE:
This. This mod right here. This one. Download it. Use it. Love it. Thank the creator and give him a big hug for it.
Also, some advice for people who are getting frustrated with the steep difficulty curve.
1. Always bring a rookie and upgrade the squad size ASAP. The more competent soldiers you have the less you have to worry about them taking a plasma round to the kneecaps. I have a good baker's dozen of guys who are at LEAST sargeants.
2. Sharpshooters. Get a couple and make SURE they have the Long Watch ability. Having a sniper or two providing cover fire for your squad can save your damn life.
3. Stop, wait, reload. If your mission doesn't have a 'finish in X turns or you're screwed' timer, don't be afraid to pause, reload your weapons, and have a few guys go into overwatch... ESPECIALLY when reinforcements are coming. There are few things greater than seeing a freshly deployed squad of Advent soldiers get torn apart by a hail of gunfire before they can get a single shot off becuase your entire squad was in overwatch waiting for them.
4. When all else fails, use fire. Grenades, rockets, etc. Don't be afraid to blow♥♥♥♥♥♥up. You might lose some stuff, but it's worth it if you can make your life easier in the long run. Blow up cover so that your other units can get a clear shot, blast an enemy to knock them out of overwatch or suppressing fire, etc. This is ESPECIALLY useful when cars, tanker trucks, or other flammable things are involved as they'll explode too and deal bonus damage. I've seen squads of sectoids and vipers rain down gently across the landscape from one well placed explosive.
5. To hell with the civvies, focus on the X-rays. Y'know those rescue missions where you can evac civilians? Civvies are♥♥♥♥♥♥at staying in cover. The best way to protect them is to kill the aliens before they can kill them. Let them run around in a panic and give ET something else to worry about, namely your friend Mr. Boomstick.
6. Sectoids die FAST AND HARD. They can mind control your guys, they can make them panic or disorient them, they can even play necromancer and bring their guys back from the dead as zombies. Kill the ♥♥♥♥ers first! Also, when they die those effects go poof with them. Very useful~
7. R&D and Communications are vital. Whenever you make contact with a new region the first thing you should always do is build a comm tower, the more you have the more supply the resistance sends you each month. Also, if you have a chance to recruit an engineer, ALWAYS take it! Engineers are key to managing your ship. The more you have the more power you'll have, the more regions you can contact, your research will go faster in the Proving Grounds, and so on. Your squad can be skilled enough to bring a tear to G.I. Joe's eye, but if they're using rubber band guns and wearing football padding for armor it won't matter.
8. Don't be afraid to restart. XCOM 2 is almost a roguelike in some respects. Don't be afraid to stop and retry with the knowledge you've gained from this playthrough. Sometimes you're backed into a corner and simply can't win. It happens.
9. The Steam Workshop is your friend. Besides the Quiet Bradford! mod (and again, big thanks to the mod's creator) there's a whole host of other useful ones I've found. Some will give rookies a small boost to aim to help even out the difficulty, some will slow or even stop the Avatar Project timer. This game is a really nasty one sometimes and there's no shame in adding a couple mods to help if its just too difficult to enjoy.

I'm gonna tell you right out the gate, fallout 4 is no where near as good as fallout 3 or fallout new Vegas from story standpoint.
I hate the way VATS performs now, I seriously hate it, it's terrible. VATS was something I almost relied upon in previous games, but here I will almost never use it. I also think the Commonwealth is the smallest map yet in a fallout game, which is another con for me. I'm noticing that I can find most of the locations in the Commonwealth in half the time it took me to in fallout 3 and new vegas.
That's the main drawback. I personally feel it also doesn't hold up as well on very specific aspects, but these are just knit picks on my part, not actual problems with the game design. Overall, this game completely anniahlates the previous 2 fallouts graphics wise, without question. That, and the introduction of settlement building are 2 of the strongest points of this game.
Another very nice touch is how they revamped entirely how power armor is utilized. In previous games it was simply a outfit  (a very heavy one) like all other outfits that could be equipped and unequipped at will. However, since it provides the best protection of anything else and was very heavy, it meant that every late game character would most likely be wearing power armor of some form. (Mainly the case of fallout 3. Fallout new Vegas had non power armor options that were on par with them.) However, in fallout 4, power armor is not a outfit, it is more like a vehicle, that needs to be fueled off a consumable power core, but gives you incredible durability and other utilities. In essence. .......power armor now feels exactly how it was meant to feel....like a suit of armor that you take care of and customize,  and take into battle, just like the knights of medieval days. And that is the way it should be from here on out.
The story, while it does carry some weight, is completely forgettable as soon as you get to diamond city. After that, it's either you pursue it further under your own willpower, or..........GATHER RESOURCES, BUILD SETTLEMENT, INSTALL NUDE MODS, EXPLORE, FIND BADASS GEAR........wait, what the F was the main story again?  Oh right,  lul -_- Someone told me this before I bought this game and let me tell you, it will certainly happen like this for most of you, the story is just not very engaging. Sure it's sad and tragic, but it's made even more tragic by the fact that 90% of us forgot about it until sometime around building our 3 settlement and managing a trade caravan empire.
Finally weapon customization, I guess it's alright, and it is time consuming, so is armor building, they are both very well implemented and offers lots of possibilities to fit each playstyle, but as far as creating anything goes, the real highlight of the game.......is settlement building and mods. These 2 things alone are what truly set fallout 4 as a game desErving of great reviews and high recognition as a great game.
Every fallout fan....should be here right now. Every newcomer, should be looking to try fallout 3 and new Vegas first, and then come here. That is the only way to truly appreciate what this game does right in my opinion, otherwise you might take it for granted. Bethesda has made yet another good game......but beware, as they may take thier success today, for granted tomorrow.

For a F2P game this has a lot going for it. While it still has a few clunks in it, it is still in Early Access so that's to be expected.
Pros:
-To start off guns are a permanent buy, it's not like those games where you have to re-buy a gun every week and they're also quite affordable. With the money that you start off with you can get 2 nice weapons with all of the attachments to them.
-Matchmaking is also pretty smooth, never had to wait more than 30 seconds for a match in any playlist
-There's a few different gametypes: TDM, Assassination (kill a VIP then escape on a helicopter), Destruction (destroy these big box things and get points), and Bomb (typical teams taking turns planting or defusing bombs).
-There's four different classes, and while they aren't terribly different, they do add some form of variety, and also any weapons can be used in any class (classes are only used in Destruction).
-Game is not intensive and you can pretty much play it with 100 fps on a toaster.
Cons:
-Switching weapons/switching between sprinting and normal movement/switching to primary after throwing a grenade takes a really long time. This eliminates running and gunning sorta because of the 2 second lag time after sprinting to the point that your gun can actually be fired, but it seems way too long especially after throwing a grenade and having to wait behind cover for a bit until you pull out your gun.
-Recoil is 100% scripted for each gun making it very easy to make a macro for a gun to shoot perfectly straight. This isn't considered "hacking" persay, but it is really annoying because someone with a 100 clip LMG that’s supposed to be inaccurate can shoot perfectly straight with only a basic knowledge of how to make a mouse macro.
-Movement in general seems a bit clumsy. Something about the way that you can turn directions really quickly, or how fluid it is when you move makes it feel wrong. But again the game is in Early Access, and I'm sure they'll be able to work on that.
-There is a special currency store with weapons in it that after looking at them for a little while definitely are better than those that you can get with the normal "gold" (which is silver but oh well), so that has the danger of becoming P2W, but as of rn it doesn't matter because nobody really has them, and they seem balanced enough.
-There are also not many maps but I’m sure they’ll come out with more so that also isn’t a problem
-The biggest con however I saved for last and it’s that this game doesn’t bring anything new to the board. It’s very similar to CS in both look and play, and also is a lot like old-school Warface PVP. So I most likely won’t be playing it much because of this, but if they stay true to the F2P model, then it has a lot of potential of becoming a good FPS game.

This is the same game as Skyrim, but in a different setting.
However, in Skyrim your choices could sometimes have meaning. Here, you have a few paths to take, and they're straight shots.
The dialogue is dull. You have a whole 4 choices at any point in your unclear dialogue shrub, as many people have complained about.
The perks system has been gutted, stuffed with the corpse of the skills system, and reanimated to pose as a good idea.
Perks are meant to be ways that the player character can bend or break the rules of the world in different ways.
Now most of those perks are missing and instead you have "increase some number that would have been in the skills menu but that thing commited suicide with two round to the back of the head."
Yes, there are some perks that do let you bend the rules, but you only get one perk per level, so you have to decide between "cool perk" and "being able to survive."
Similarly, you can use perk points to increase any and all of your SPECIAL.
No, not a limited amount, like the "Extra SPECIAL" perk. All of them, all the way up to 10.
Thus your character turns into a Mary Sue. They have no limits. They can do anything and everything.
A more personal gripe now.
The compass is, by all accounts, the Skyrim compass with a different texture.
That is, enemies only show as red blips when they are aware of your presence.
That may not sound like a bad thing, but allow me to explain.
The PipBoy has various features, and one of them is the identification, and classification, of potential hostiles. Non-hostiles, the normal HUD color. Hostiles, red.
The PipBoy has this feature in the game universe, and it has been removed from this game because somebody decided to just use the Skyrim assets.
In short, this is not a Fallout game. This is a fever dream of the Dovahkin.

I've been slowly crawling my way through this game and enjoying it a ton.  It's challenging and engaging with an aesthetic you can practically taste.  I've lost countless heroes and been tragically unlucky at the most important of moments.  It is only now, on Week 115 of my Campaign, that I finally say, "♥♥♥♥ this game in it's gaping RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."
On my way to defeat the last Boss on my list before delving into the Darkest Dungeon itself, I chose a group of hardy warriors, having proven themselves more than capable countless times.  I knew full well it was more than likely that they would not return.
However, their trek through the ruins seemed to be going remarkably well, and having cleared the last room before the Boss in question, they were all at full health and less than 10 stress.  I rested, buffed my team as best I could, and sent them off down the hallway towards their foe and, mayhaps, victory.
What they met was calamity and disaster.
The very first step into the halls saw them set upon by a common array of rabble, except for one little addition; a Doomsayer.  Hoping to kill him quickly, as they all to easily overwhelm the weak with their cursed words, I let loose the Houndmaster, Arbalest, and Hellion.  On the fifth turn, they were finally able to land a single blow.  He dodged 12 attacks in a row.  That single blow thankfully killed him, but the party was now in rough shape, and two of them dangerously close to having their resolve tested.  I bought some time to patch everyone up, and they moved ever forward once again...
Into an unburnt torch, and them into a Collector.
Who seemed intent on constantly summoning two Man-At-Arms to keep him Guarded.
But they won, and an array of crits kept my party whole but at half health across the board.  My Hellion needed only the smallest nudge to possibly lose herself, and the Vestal close behind.  The next step down the hall was blessedly empty, and I made the call to use the rest of my food to patch up the weakest of the party.
This proved to be folly, as their hunger decided to strike in the few moments before their final encounter.  They took 20% health damage, and my Hellion failed her resolve and turned to be Selfish.
Yet somehow, through Marks and luck, I was able to savagly set upon the Gibbering Prophet, reducing him to 52hp very quickly, and it seemed as though victory would be achieved despite the pitfalls.
I was sorely mistaken.
The Houndmaster hit him for 24, but resisted the Bleed.  The Hellion had done as she was instructed this entire time, but failed to cooperate in the last two turns before her demise to a tick of Blight on Deathsdoor, which was fair.  Arbalest hits for 18, Vestal is constantly spamming the area heal to keep everyone from deaths door, and I've finally run out of the stack of cures for Blight I brought with me.  The Prophet sets up the attack that will drop both the Houndmaster and Hellion to nill.
Hellion dies, Hound hits for 7 (somehow), Prophet resists the bleed, kills the Houndmaster, and leaves the Vestal and Arbalest right up front and my only prayer of doing those last 3HP of damage being Blind Fire and moving the Vestal to take the hits from above to buy him more time.
Now earlier, having my progress going to well, I took out one of the Wooden Pews for the extra gold because I'm always hurting for it pretty bad, and I counter myself lucky that I had one less target for it to randomly choose.
I somehow lasted another four turns and not once did he strike the Boss.
Now all of these things are to be expected in this game, and it is as harsh and unforgiving as it claims to be, but it is no longer worth my time to trudge through it.  I have failed my resolve test, and so ♥♥♥♥ this game.

Review from 2/4/2016 to 2/8/2016
TL;DR XCOM 2 meets and exceeds all the gameplay standards of its predecessor. But the graphics performance is horrendous and ruins gameplay experience. Do not buy this game until they fix it.
Full Review
XCOM 2 meets all the gameplay standards of its predecessor. There's simply more of everything in terms of choices, but strategically still works quite elegantly.  The concealment phase / ambush mechanic was my favorite addition.  Though I'm glad they took out the interceptor mini-game and expanded the world map (instead of just satellites) I was a little sad by the lack of Avenger customization. Too straight forward.
Graphically, the game is quite beautiful.  Art, design, and story are all great.
But seriously, was this game even tested? The game constantly hangs and freezes. The last level alone was hell on Earth.  I was forced to lower settings to Minimal and it was still chugging.  Everytime reinforcements came in, I had to pray to Sid Meier that the game wouldn't crash.
I understand the realities of software engineering and the difficult problems that arise, especially for a PC title.  But the lack of polish makes XCOM 2 a sub-AAA game or not worth the price.

+1year after release consider this the final patched version.
PVP is very disappointing and frustrating with broken hitboxes, laggy matchmaking (or netcode ?) and overall unsatisfying fight dynamic.
NPC quests, (inexistent)-storytelling and lore presentation really don't do it for me.
PVE and map design is bland and non innovative. Most bosses are forgettable.
Faster gameplay is a step in the right direction but it feels like a circus at times, Bloodborne did it better.
Unfinished and/or rushed ? Where are previous improvements from Dark Souls 2 ?
I still have a sour taste from the Dark Souls 2 Scholar of the first sin rerelease and this last adventure doesn't end with a glorious note. No interest for DLC.
-PVP- Focused on 1v1, invasions
Longswords hit 1m away from their tip, lance charges have a 2m radius despite the animation, phantom hits through evasion rolls, 180 degrees correction turns ala ballerina (non commiting start animation).
Poise system is ineffective (balance stat granted by armor) so a walking mountain ends up being staggered by a plastic butter knife 3 meters away thanks to cross-continental lag. You often trade direct blows despite having a clearly faster windup or longer range. There is also a hyperarmor granted upon swinging certain heavy weapons which grants stagger immunity however this starts too early in the swinging animation e.g. R1 > first horizontal swing ends > R1 > opponent fails to stagger you whilst you're not even in a swinging animation (sword is still held to the side) due to R1 prefire. 2 light attacks should chain into each other but lag sets them free at times ending up in a trade.
Parries do not make for an interesting/fun fight or mechanic, certain movesets are so telegraphed (limited melee mixups) you might as well stop there once you see a buckler rise up. With this well established lag I refuse to believe parrying is a worhful tactic in PVP.
Class balance relies mostly on offensive tools thus magic or weapons. Most spells are telegraphed once again but maybe you could catch a lucky lag rollback into your AoE. Hyperarmor heavy weapons and overreaching longswords/estoc are clearly superior, lagwarrior trumping all. I used a scythe which wasn't high tier.
Too much stamina regen and too many rolls making matches often devolve into a circus poke and run (if you're not abusing hyperarmor). Fighting games rounds usually finish under 45sec and are a lot more action packed.
Matchmaking balance is also lacking as you'll encounter during your early adventure many geared-up opponents with end-game accessories. Or hackers corrupting your save ! This matchmaking cannot be taken seriously when Western Europe is being matched against China/Taiwan/South Africa, even at EU prime time and correct networking options (which don't appear to achieve anything).
PVP activities seem unfinised with 2 covenants (guilds) being the same in practice : Darkmoon and Blue Sentinels. They also both struggle to get any action it turns out (which DS2 handled better). No big innovations with the others. Arena __locked__ to a DLC !!!
Coming from fighting games this PVP community doesn't feel welcoming. Lot of snarky behavior (hatemail, salt miners, griefing, tryhards) and a ever weird cult of memes and antics. I'll never get those emotes...
Overall gameplay quality really feels unrefined due to the points above. If you like 1v1 technical dueling see fighting games, if you like small group brawling see MMORPG Dota or what have you. Dark Souls weapon dynamic really isn't that interesting.
For example fighting games have :
- clear and consistent data, rules and animations/hitboxes = when I do this action this __should__ happen everytime
- low inputlag and hopefully better regional/rank matchmaking
- technical with pressure, mixups, low/overhead, jumping, grabs, oki, reactions, meters, reversal and combos
- fast dynamic and fluid
- mostly balanced and no gear/build time waste
- fighting space management (additional pressure once cornered)
- easier on the eyes, an arena focuses on the fighters with clear animations / chara design (it's hard to identify dark souls weapons at times)
- no silly mile staring contest whilst jiggling around, 9 consecutive circus rolls or improvised marathon. There is always a reaction button to press for pressure/punish
- no roleplay no gimmicks, just people punching each other to death as it should be
-NPC, story and lore- SPOILERS
I hate Dark Souls 3 friendly NPC with a burning passion. Their quests are hidden, nonsensical or cryptic which means you'll most likely have to play with the wiki on your lap. Many annoying branches or death ends with one benign action messing up a whole quest progression. And their voice lines... Heheeeee, hahahaaaa, siiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiight at every dialogue end. Their mysterious faked relevance feels so forced.
See the Catarina knight for example (which you meet at Undead Settlement), you end up tricked in the Cathedral by Patches wearing a Catarina armor and somehow have to guess he stole it from the knight now trapped in a well you're very likely to never pass again ? This ain't a unique armor why would have I made the connection ?
Or Sirris which hates me for taking Rosaria's fingers. You couldn't deduct it from her previous dialogue at all.
Only cool guy is Greirat and he ended up killed, thank you From Software.
First time I met Emma the old lady guarding Lothric Castle I sliced her open in frustration before the end of her lines. This is the first NPC alluding to the story and she ends up pulling a banner out of her bottom for an inexistent and unexplained plot. That's all she is just a banner butt-puller, MMORPG Fedex quest throwbacks anyone ? Some swear by this storytelling or lack thereof, I think it's lazy. A MMORPG has more of a story and NPC development. Dark Souls 1 sitting knight at the shrine at least gave you some useful indications.
External forums lorefagging is not a valid form of storytelling (neither for mechanics explanation !!! see poise). Sparsed hints (willfully left cryptic so up to open interpretation) aren't either.
-PVE- SPOILERS
Muddy swamp, catacombs and generic skeletons, fire hell, cathedral, they really didn't look far for innovation.
Some segments really made me scratch my head : first part from Road of Sacrifices with the Corvian felt off for example.
Lothric castle looks good I suppose. Graphics and lighting feel nice.
Seeing most of the map is a welcome return from the first game.
Most bosses are forgettable. Yhorm is the worst boss fight I've ever experienced making me question if it was designed by totally unrelated developpers, it's supposed to be one of the 4 capital bosses dammit ! Abyss watchers is laughably weak to stagger so keep your table spoon at hand ! Deacons of the Deep and Skeleton Lord Wulnir are trash mob worthy, Should you meet oversized or hyperactive monsters it's the awful camera (5th game still not right) you'll fight instead.
Lothric Princes were frustrating due to teleportation (causes loss of camera tracking, can end up behind you so off screen) into bright flash covering up the followup animation. It's a fun fight otherwise.
I wished they explored some new modes or PVE covenants, a boss rush could have been fun.
I'll be honest Dark Souls 3 left me quite bitter, playing with a blood dagger staggering everything whilst iframe drifting felt ridiculous. Previously mentionned sections didn't help. Lord of the Cinder probably saved the experience as he is the best boss fight (or one of) I've ever encountered. A boss made up of all players with all fighting styles, aggresive fast and opportunistic AI (I swear that guy surprised me with his onpoint Oki, miracle force or lance circling swings). Clear and well made patterns. Sound design and arena were great. I catched some funny pop offs when he got my character down, showing off his mighty blows to the cameraman (double miracle force for example).
Great game, has LOTS of potential. even though that it is still in beta, its pretty fun

The 5v5 and 8v8 modes are really really good, the other ones(excluding Assassination) are pure garbage and i wouldnt step close to them except maybe classic TDM if you like running and gunning. This review is for the competitive modes in the game
Pros:
-Great Visuals(great animations and environment, like seriously the animators are amazing)
-Good gameplay and unique mechanics
-Competitive maps are well designed and have good attack/defend balance
-very good map variety
-Quick intense rounds
Cons:
-Guns are not all available and may seem pay to win to some
To expand on this: It is NOT pay to win, the default weapons are good and can be used to kill players who paid for weapons, the only issue I see here is that the snipers are not as easily obtainable as the other weapon types and are potiential one hit kills making them strong against new players
-too much health(at times it may seem like someone can soak bullets and not die, damage needs a bit of tweaking other than the snipers and the pistols)
-Not huge variety of weapons(4 main types and 2 that are all too similar)
-No voice coms
-Players move too fast compared to the knife, the base speed needs to be lowerd when you dont have the knife out
-No map pref in casual play
-Crouching is too fast, I cannot stress this enough, slow down the 3rd person crouch animation to match the 1st person speed
I would recommend it as a poor mans counter-strike but some of the mechanics are well done in this and really stick out compared to CS(example: the lasers that arent shown to your enemy, it allows no negative competitive edge and is a good tool to see where your team is watching especially without coms making it easier to work together. I would recommend making it so the laser is not visible but the dot is so there is a downside created). Is it just as competitive? No, due to no economy and also weapons arent all available. Does that mean its worse than CS? No they are different games that have different gameplay with similar mechanics. CS has been around a long time and nailed alot of things because of it. Honestly its a fun game that needs polishing.
To the devs: Dont add that girl character thats in the trailer in the short shorts, dear god that trailer is bad. The trailer really turned me off and made me question the game, The only reason I got it is because in the game description you boasted good netcode and anticheat with no pay2win, that shows alot of care in your game wether you realise it or not.
7/10 Needs polishing but great for a free2play

"Such a dank and dismal place these warrens be," spoke Arthus the Crusader, "Yet we delve here to purge it of these abominations."
The path ahead was not only dank and dismal, but a path walked only by those who seek death. For the monsters within the warrens were not meant for the mortal realm.
Darkest Dungeons is a rogue-like dungeon explorer. The map is always changing as you explore several different areas from the Warrens to the Wealds. Your party of adventures, currently 28 in all, depart in groups of 4 into these devious places. Lepers, Crusaders, Vestals, and more join your party at the hamlet, the last sanction of humanity in the estate of your grandfather.

And while you can stock your parties with torches, food, and other items; none of these can prepare the adventurers like experience. For each successful journey will reward your parties with resolve, providing benefits and afflictions with each level. Disease, phobias, and more can infect your adventurers, but can be removed for a cost.
Darkest Dungeon is an excellent game. It makes you think. It makes you take risk. Each delve into the dungeons comes with a chance of glorious rewards. The atmosphere of the game really sells it, making each delve a dark journey into the unknown. Between the traps, monsters, and other events, Darkest Dungeon really gives some interesting challenges. With the more recent updates adding new classes, fixing mechanics, and removing bugs; it's really come together as a great game.
I highly recommend Darkest Dungeon if you want a challenging game with an eldritch horror vibe to it.

I'll start with a warning: If you dislike RNG and it making a big difference, you might wanna skip this game. Even with the right tactics, some well-geared characters and a lot of experience, some encounters might still get your favorite adventurers killed. You should be aware of this, and if you hate having some very unhappy rolls on attacks, then this might be very frustrating.
Now... I at first wasn't very interest in DD, but a review and stream by TB made me change my mind and try it. And I was captivated quickly. The game is a LOT of fun.
The graphics and animations are very simple, but also, very stylish, so they have character and are nice to look at.
The atmosphere is great. There is a certain Lovecraftian vibe to things (not only because madness can become a real problem for your adventurers), and the narrator does SUCH a great job (BTW, check out his readings of HPL-stories, such a cool experience).
Even with a lot of training, these dungeons will be risky for your guys. Bad RNG on heals (instead of, say, 8 points, you get 0 or 1 points, which means you kinda lost a turn) or damage (sometimes, you are THAT close to killing a mob, but then, 2-3 of your guys actually MISS, and you actually end up losing), debuffs like selfishness (your character might snag loot for himself), or paranoia (he or she might actually REFUSE to be healed) etc.
I did like the darkness-mechanic. There are advantages and disadvantages to letting the light go dim or using torches to get to 100 light. With this mechanic, you kinda pick how you wanna approach the dungeon, a little bit like controlling the difficulty level yourself (not that it is a cakewalk if you spam torches, mind you!), and the increased rewards you get for fights at low light levels come with increased risks too.
So, you may ask, why do people play this? Are we all out for punishment? No! The game is just very addictive in that "Come on, just one more quick dungeon before I head to bed... whoops, it's 3 AM?!?!" way.
It is challenging, it will often feel unfair, but boy, winning battles and completing dungeons feels so very satisfying. You start to care about your chars (and there is an achievement about beating the final boss with the chars you get at the beginning of the game), especially if you name them yourself.
A guide might help you get started, as money will be an issue (supplies are expensive, so you wanna pick carefully what to take along), but even if you just dive in and go trial and error, you will learn what to do.
Talking about that, here is one complaint I have: The supplies and treatments IMO are TOO expensive. Even when you clear out tons of tough dungeons, you might have low funds due to the prize of upgrades to your buildings, treatments and supplies like bandages and torches. Sure, those supplies shouldnt be so cheap or plentiful that you can spam them at all times, but then, simply limit the amount you can get more. I didn't mind all the bad luck with the RNG and losing fights I thought I'd rather easily win, but I found those prizes frustrating, and IMO, they should be lowered at least a tiny bit.
Other than that: It's a great, tactical game, some fights will have you bite your nails, sometimes you will feel disappointed, especially when losing a character you leveled up. The game will eventually become kinda grindy, but at that point, you could just play it casually, like doing half an hour or so and then returning later.
Pros:
- Atmospheric
- Simple, but unique graphics and animations
- Great narrator voice
- Challenging
- You get to choose your ability-loadout
- Very satisfying when you beat a boss or dungeon...
CONS
...and very frustrating when they beat YOU
- Expensive supplies
- Expensive treatment to get rid of debuffs and stuff
- Can get grindy
- Not recommended if you hate losing RNG rolls even when your characters are leveled and equipped with good gear
- Can feel a bit repetitive

Review from 2/4/2016 to 2/8/2016
TL;DR XCOM 2 meets and exceeds all the gameplay standards of its predecessor. But the graphics performance is horrendous and ruins gameplay experience. Do not buy this game until they fix it.
Full Review
XCOM 2 meets all the gameplay standards of its predecessor. There's simply more of everything in terms of choices, but strategically still works quite elegantly.  The concealment phase / ambush mechanic was my favorite addition.  Though I'm glad they took out the interceptor mini-game and expanded the world map (instead of just satellites) I was a little sad by the lack of Avenger customization. Too straight forward.
Graphically, the game is quite beautiful.  Art, design, and story are all great.
But seriously, was this game even tested? The game constantly hangs and freezes. The last level alone was hell on Earth.  I was forced to lower settings to Minimal and it was still chugging.  Everytime reinforcements came in, I had to pray to Sid Meier that the game wouldn't crash.
I understand the realities of software engineering and the difficult problems that arise, especially for a PC title.  But the lack of polish makes XCOM 2 a sub-AAA game or not worth the price.

I have a feeling that people who complain about the game being "unfair and random" are just not very good at it, and can't accept that sometimes you WILL lose and people WILL die, because you can't savescum. The game is challenging and fun to play, moreover it has an amazing visual and audio design, it oozes atmosphere all the time, and the addition of the narrator (oh my god his voice is so good) was a great idea.
I have never felt like I was presented with a challenge I couldn't overcome, even later in the game when the dunbgeons are supposed to be "impossible" and "unfair". They really aren't. you just can't go in blindly and expect to win with every team. Figure out what works and what doesn't in each dungeon, design your team accordingly. Sometimes you will get screwed by dice rolls, sure. But it's part of the course, just as it is part of the course in games like Xcom, it's all about minimizing the risks. If one bad dice roll puts you in the losing position, you are doing something wrong.
The game is hard and mean, and is not going to cut you any slack. The last dungeon is a huge difficulty spike, but it's nowhere near impossible. It's (again) all about figuring out what works and what doesn't, if you keep bashing your head against the wall, maybe it's time to rethink your approach, instead of going to the internet to complain?
The game is awesome, but not for people who want to succeed every time they play, that's not how it works. If you can't tolerate the fact that the game has some random elements that work for and against you, then this is not a game for you.

For a game that fairly new, as well as being in early access, its a great game! And also Considering the fact that this game is free, I think that this game is awesome! It is not P2W (Pay to Win). In fact, I only could find 1 way you could pay, and the premium currecny is only for skins! For Simplicity sake, I will show the Pros and Cons
-Pros-
~It's Free
~NOT P2W (there is a use for Premium currency, but only for skins and stuff)
~You can use Iron sights
~good variety of Game Modes
~Not super High computer Requirements, yet still looks nice (Unreal Engine 3 For The Win!)
~Not a lot of Glitches
~Only an 11 Gig download
~Playing with friends is really simple, and not that complicated
~No sign up
~Steady servers (they don't crash)
~Adding more content :D
~No OP weapons, overall very balanced
~Developers actually care
-Cons- (most of these are minor issues)
~limited customisation
~Very Limited amount of weapons you can use (just added a couple of more in the last update)
~Only 3 available customizable loadouts (I know thats about the standard, but wish there was 1 or 2 more)
~unless you log in everyday and do the challenges, you will grind heavily
~Some maps feel unbalanced
~some lag spikes during gameplay
~Hackers are not that uncommon, and no anti-cheat system, or even a report option :/
~gernade launchers don't do enough damage in my opinion (they are not noob tubes, so thats good, but you could survive getting hit dead on with a gernade launcher)

~Noticable typos and a poor sense of grammar
But hey, For an Early Access Game, this is really good. Hopefully we will see an update that will give us some more content! The challenges help you with grinding, and you start out with 200K gold, which is enough to buy you at least any 1 weapon of your choice! But because this game is early access, things might be prone to change, and My review may vary, but for now, I would highly reccomend getting this game!

I haven't quite done everything that can be done in the game so I don't exactly have a complete experience, even remotely... but I will say that it is well worth the money if you want an interesting survival based somewhat sandbox game. This has fewer sandbox elements however, and leans towards and objective. The main comparison people draw this to is of course Terraria. I enjoy both a lot. Terraria I love because unlike minecraft, there is a chain of events. Although there is no story to terraria, you cannot experience MANY things of the game until you complete some kind of prerequisite milestone, like hard mode for example. It gave Terraria a great many things that Minecraft doesn't do well on as well as blowing it out of the water with it's many unique boss fights.
Starbound has one thing that I have noticed that is a major difference to Terraria though, and that is the thing that I love the most about Starbound..... YOU ARE NOT CONSTANTLY UNDER ATTACK BY MOBS!!!! -.-
This killed many things for me in Terraria. Sure it's fun as hell though, but you never get a break from monster attacks and hardly get to breathe before the next encounter. Even if you seal yourself off, a chaos elemental might just pop in it and kill you, so you die anyway. When hosting a Terraria server? Forget it, never even THINK about going afk. Everytime I did in particularly there was a Blood Moon lol.
So bottom line about Starbound now, aside from my incomplete experience is that you can take the game at your own pace. This makes life so much easier for everyone. Designated spots have monsters in them so you aren't always under attack. There IS indeed an objective, and from I've seen there are apparently skills and a strange level-up system. It's not with exp though, but apparently it is based by the gear you wear. The game is what it is, an experience. Try it out yourself because in my own opinion 15 bucks is a steal for games of this quality

Darkest Dungeon is a strange game (but in a good way if you read further and peruse my reasoning).
It's a gritty dark fantasy adventure set in an undetermined time. You act as an overseer who recruits motely crews of adventurers to unearth relics (and whatever isn't nailed down) from the ruins of your ancestors' lands. Unfortunately one of your ancestors dealt too far into the occult, unleashing some horror which wears down on the resolve and sanity of your heroes (that's where the Lovecraftian stuff comes into play).
Seems fair enough, and enough of a reason to get into it and play it. What makes this game strange is the idea that failure isn't only a possibility, but inevitable. The grim, gritty atmosphere isn't only in the graphics (which are beautiful, inspiring, and decadent at the same time), but in the gameplay and feelings evoked by this game. Expeditions into the ruins of your ancestors will fail, and death/madness is a likely prospect given that your adventurers have both HP and stress to manage throughout the game.
Gameplay wise, it plays as a party rogue-like with turn-based combat. There is copious strategy to be discovered and applied as you unearth the ruins and build a competent enough team to assault the 'Darkest Dungeon'. To prepare your hired cohorts, you can find relics and family heirlooms in the various parts of the manor's surrounding lands to help upgrade the hub village you use to rest and arm your hirelings. With these heirlooms, you upgrade the various businesses and buildings: upgrading the blacksmith allows you to better arm your (surviving) heroes. Upgrading the Inn enables your unhinged heroes to restore their sanity by taking their mind off the oppresive atmosphere via gambling, drinking, and of course whoring. Your more pious heroes benefit from the chapel, which allows them the option of prayer or sacrifice to hopefully assist in recovering their resolve. A sanitarium acts as both a mental ward and hospital to cure your hirelings of any debilitating diseases or psychosis. Even outside of battle and dungeon-delving, there's enough strategy in managing your town that any contemplative RPG-Strategy players will be satisfied.
Unfortunately, the biggest gripe that I have is the early-stage grind required to build a competent team. Experience is only gained through successful runs through the dungeon, and not at an encounter basis, meaning a failed mission merely leaves you with a bunch of insane heroes and little treasure. That would be fine, but items can only be upgraded if the hireling's level matches the item's strength. And unfortunately, most dungeons increase in diffculty and strength as you complete them (regardless of the heroes you might have in reserve), meaning that one bad run due to a very cruel and unforgiving random number generator can easily wipe out your best and well-armed heroes, leaving you with level 0 hirelings to face the same threats your A-team took on. This ends up adding hours, effectively bashing your head into the wall, and sending heroes through the meat-grinder until the dice ends up rolling in your favor. That idea alone can be very discouraging.
Still, if you are a fan of atmosphere and of the belief that it's persistence that wins you the day, then Darkest Dungeon is a worthwhile purchase and a memorable game experience! 4 out of 5.

The main character is voice acted, but so was Witcher 3 and we all know how successful that game was.  Voice acting aside, this game has a fairly long main questline with three main factions, each with their own set of morals that impose some tough decisions on the player, as well as a few well hidden plot twists.  I concede that the voice acting is a little rough around the edges, but it definetly isn't worth trashing this entire game over.
True to the Bethesda spirit the world is packed with interesting locations, things to see, and quests to complete.  If you liked walking around Skyrim simply for the sake of exploring, then this game will not disappoint. Say good bye to the sepia and green filters that smothered the colors of previous games: the wastes of this game actually look kinda nice considering what they are.  And with a fancy GPU one can explore the wastes in high detail.
My main annoyance with this game, as always with bethesda games, is the combat can be a little tiresome. Since each enemy has a different weakness, I have to expend over half my inventory space accomodating a collection of weapons, each for a certain situation: long range, medium range, indoors, outdoors, melee, armor piercing, bombs, lasers, etc. I can't even carry around my beloved Fat Man at all times because I need to collect desk fans.
Final thoughts: Don't get caught up comparing this game to New Vegas. I played New Vegas and they are two completely different games.

I'm gonna tell you right out the gate, fallout 4 is no where near as good as fallout 3 or fallout new Vegas from story standpoint.
I hate the way VATS performs now, I seriously hate it, it's terrible. VATS was something I almost relied upon in previous games, but here I will almost never use it. I also think the Commonwealth is the smallest map yet in a fallout game, which is another con for me. I'm noticing that I can find most of the locations in the Commonwealth in half the time it took me to in fallout 3 and new vegas.
That's the main drawback. I personally feel it also doesn't hold up as well on very specific aspects, but these are just knit picks on my part, not actual problems with the game design. Overall, this game completely anniahlates the previous 2 fallouts graphics wise, without question. That, and the introduction of settlement building are 2 of the strongest points of this game.
Another very nice touch is how they revamped entirely how power armor is utilized. In previous games it was simply a outfit  (a very heavy one) like all other outfits that could be equipped and unequipped at will. However, since it provides the best protection of anything else and was very heavy, it meant that every late game character would most likely be wearing power armor of some form. (Mainly the case of fallout 3. Fallout new Vegas had non power armor options that were on par with them.) However, in fallout 4, power armor is not a outfit, it is more like a vehicle, that needs to be fueled off a consumable power core, but gives you incredible durability and other utilities. In essence. .......power armor now feels exactly how it was meant to feel....like a suit of armor that you take care of and customize,  and take into battle, just like the knights of medieval days. And that is the way it should be from here on out.
The story, while it does carry some weight, is completely forgettable as soon as you get to diamond city. After that, it's either you pursue it further under your own willpower, or..........GATHER RESOURCES, BUILD SETTLEMENT, INSTALL NUDE MODS, EXPLORE, FIND BADASS GEAR........wait, what the F was the main story again?  Oh right,  lul -_- Someone told me this before I bought this game and let me tell you, it will certainly happen like this for most of you, the story is just not very engaging. Sure it's sad and tragic, but it's made even more tragic by the fact that 90% of us forgot about it until sometime around building our 3 settlement and managing a trade caravan empire.
Finally weapon customization, I guess it's alright, and it is time consuming, so is armor building, they are both very well implemented and offers lots of possibilities to fit each playstyle, but as far as creating anything goes, the real highlight of the game.......is settlement building and mods. These 2 things alone are what truly set fallout 4 as a game desErving of great reviews and high recognition as a great game.
Every fallout fan....should be here right now. Every newcomer, should be looking to try fallout 3 and new Vegas first, and then come here. There's so much good about this game I'm not sure where to start... But I'll do my best.
First of all, the game has fantastic storytelling and narration. The meloncholy voice confessing his sins and warning you about what might be ahead really leaves you in a sense of suspense, and it really keeps that dark, end of the world type of tone in the game, where you otherwise might just think "Oh it's time to skip into the dungeon and loot it again!"
Second of all, the game is, for the most part, very fair. People often complain about RNG, but this often causes their defeat because they become too comfortable with smooth runs, and aren't prepared for the worst when it finally happens. While a hero dying is permanent, you'll often be given so many chances to save them. A hero can
been one-shot, in
circumstance. Instead, they enter death's door, where every hit beyond that has a chance to kill them permanently(If you want to understand this mechanic further, please research it online, there's plenty of info.)
Thirdly, the art. The art looks fantastic! It really drips with that Lovecraftian feel. The characters all look really unique, and the locations are as eerie as ever.
Of course, the game also comes with the unique stress system. While it is the idea that's supposed to keep the game so unique and seperate from others, it actually feels more like a secondary health bar. You try to keep it under control, and it will sometimes require maintenance outside of the dungeon, because your heroes do not instantly go to 0 stress after a mission, while they will fully heal afterwards(odd, eh?)
The only negative thing I can say about the game is that it feels like it hangs around a little longer than neccessary. With a lot of skill, you can clear the game in a reletively short time, but the endgame is
difficult, and unless you find the information online, will probably consist of some trial-and-error. The problem is, because the permadeath, you'll find yourself having to re-train heroes from step 1 to retry the final dungeon. This can make the length feel a bit inflated for anyone unable to overcome that final hurdle.
Overall, I'd say the game is fantastic, though I bought it on sale, I feel it was completely worth $15.
PS: I normally despise turn-based games that don't involve 3D movement.

Darkest Dungeon is a strange game (but in a good way if you read further and peruse my reasoning).
It's a gritty dark fantasy adventure set in an undetermined time. You act as an overseer who recruits motely crews of adventurers to unearth relics (and whatever isn't nailed down) from the ruins of your ancestors' lands. Unfortunately one of your ancestors dealt too far into the occult, unleashing some horror which wears down on the resolve and sanity of your heroes (that's where the Lovecraftian stuff comes into play).
Seems fair enough, and enough of a reason to get into it and play it. What makes this game strange is the idea that failure isn't only a possibility, but inevitable. The grim, gritty atmosphere isn't only in the graphics (which are beautiful, inspiring, and decadent at the same time), but in the gameplay and feelings evoked by this game. Expeditions into the ruins of your ancestors will fail, and death/madness is a likely prospect given that your adventurers have both HP and stress to manage throughout the game.
Gameplay wise, it plays as a party rogue-like with turn-based combat. There is copious strategy to be discovered and applied as you unearth the ruins and build a competent enough team to assault the 'Darkest Dungeon'. To prepare your hired cohorts, you can find relics and family heirlooms in the various parts of the manor's surrounding lands to help upgrade the hub village you use to rest and arm your hirelings. With these heirlooms, you upgrade the various businesses and buildings: upgrading the blacksmith allows you to better arm your (surviving) heroes. Upgrading the Inn enables your unhinged heroes to restore their sanity by taking their mind off the oppresive atmosphere via gambling, drinking, and of course whoring. Your more pious heroes benefit from the chapel, which allows them the option of prayer or sacrifice to hopefully assist in recovering their resolve. A sanitarium acts as both a mental ward and hospital to cure your hirelings of any debilitating diseases or psychosis. Even outside of battle and dungeon-delving, there's enough strategy in managing your town that any contemplative RPG-Strategy players will be satisfied.
Unfortunately, the biggest gripe that I have is the early-stage grind required to build a competent team. Experience is only gained through successful runs through the dungeon, and not at an encounter basis, meaning a failed mission merely leaves you with a bunch of insane heroes and little treasure. That would be fine, but items can only be upgraded if the hireling's level matches the item's strength. And unfortunately, most dungeons increase in diffculty and strength as you complete them (regardless of the heroes you might have in reserve), meaning that one bad run due to a very cruel and unforgiving random number generator can easily wipe out your best and well-armed heroes, leaving you with level 0 hirelings to face the same threats your A-team took on. This ends up adding hours, effectively bashing your head into the wall, and sending heroes through the meat-grinder until the dice ends up rolling in your favor. That idea alone can be very discouraging.
Still, if you are a fan of atmosphere and of the belief that it's persistence that wins you the day, then Darkest Dungeon is a worthwhile purchase and a memorable game experience! 4 out of 5.

An excellent addition to the already stellar precedessor. Not only does it improve the gameplay in pretty much any way, it also introduces a number of new enemies, objectives and makes the "overworld" gameplay a lot less boring (you can actually lose the campaign now without losing any missions, which is cool).
Unfortunately, it is not a perfect game, and people with less than powerful rigs will feel how badly optimized the graphics are. While I do think most of these issues will be sorted out with time, it is a bit underwhelming to see several bugs and optimization issues on such a huge game at launch.
Also, beware of the difficulty. This game is absolutely brutal, punishes every mistake and always drives a hard bargain with the mission timers. If you are used to Enemy Unknown/Within, you have to drastically adapt your playstyle to mission timers, something which a lot of players struggle with at the moment (and they let out their anger by giving negative reviews sadly).
All in all, if you don't hate strategy or turn-based games, I would definitely recommend this game. It is one of the best strategy games of the last years, and highly addictive.

This game is indeed hard, but not as hard as people say it is.
Playing cautiously is the key to mastering this game. Chances are, if you dive into the game expecting the fast-paced action of modern games, you will put yourself into the position of being punished by ambushes and traps. Yes, the enemies can be tough to deal with, but there are multiple methods to take care of them.
This is true for single-player experiences. It is a completely different matter in the multiplayer aspect of the game.
Multiplayer:
Take what I said about being cautious, but add enemy players to the mix. Now be extremely cautious.
If you don't want to deal with invaders (players who join your game to kill you), don't be under an ember. Commit suicide to lose your ember. There are many ways to to kill yourslef in firelink shrine which is the safe area.
If you want to play with friends, expect more invasions.
What makes the game fun:
For me, it was the sense of progression. The game is set-up in a way so that as you get through the game, you notice your character getting stronger. Whether it's because you leveled up your stats or found better equipment, enemies that you had trouble with earlier are push-overs later. Not to mention, you get cooler looking equipment the further you go.
Claymore = Basic slow swings --> Greatsword = Still slow, but more damage --> Farron Greatsword = Laws of physics be damned!
Don't be ashamed of using guides for this game. Many items are hidden and require prior knowledge to collect. Quests such as the "Lord of Hollows" do not tell you how to get from point A to point B.
Is the game worth the full price-tag treatment? Well, no. $60 and more for DLC is overpriced for any one game. But, if a sale comes on for the deluxe edition that is less than $60, then you should buy it immediatly.
