Very unique and generally outstanding game; though not for the faint of heart. It's soul-crushingly brutal, at times it makes you want to just quit and never come back, though the promise of riches and glory is hard to pass up.
The atmosphere is amazing for a side-scroller, absolutely incredible voice acting from the narrator. The music while in my opinion less impressive than the narrator's voice acting, still adds a very fitting touch of dreary hopelessness and despair; the ambience, though subtle, also reinforces that.
In terms of gameplay, it's fairly standard by way of RPGs, kill monsters, collect items, upgrade your characters; however as you probably already know there is a significant emphasis on managing the mental health of your heroes, in addition the traditional system of physical health. It is in part this system that adds an additional layer of brutal difficulty to the game.
Especially when starting out, you'll be wanting to upgrade a lot of different things; the problem however is that resources and gold are scarce, so you'll have to think carefully about where you get the most bang for your buck. This ties in very well with preserving the mental health of your heroes. If you spend resources to alleviate one hero of his problems, another hero, or even multiple heroes will have to forego certain upgrades or medical treatment. The game often forces you to throw certain heroes under the bus, and then blames you for their fate, which simply further adds to the atmosphere and difficulty, both of which is exactly what the game is about.
If you're looking for a brutal RPG gaming experience that isn't Dark Souls, I would definitely recommend you try out Darkest Dungeon.
On a final note, there are many many many critics of this game, some are completely insane (obviously they cracked under the pressure of the Darkest Dungeon) and some have fair enough points. That said, many of those critics, criticize the game for it's difficulty, either directly, or in some cases indirectly, but just because they prefer their gaming experiences on a silver platter, doesn't necessarily mean everyone else does, even if they can't fathom that. My point is, do watch out for some of the negative reviews, or at least think about what they're CLAIMING an extra time, especially some of the older ones.

As a fan of minecraft and rpgs in general the moment I saw the trailer I knew I had to try this game out, and without a doubt fullfilled my expectations.
Pros :

This is just my opinion and normally I wouldn't be bothered to speak up, but quite frankly the game is getting neg bombed for a crappy reason.
Short story long....
If you like open world post apocolyptic shooters with a ton of stuff to explore and a bit of settlement minecraft added on top, this is the game for you.
Its a bit light in the RPG department if you are looking for in depth character development.  On the other hand, what is here is very close to being well done without all the stat punishment for mistakes made during day one choicemaking.  Where they dropped the ball was not including the SPECIAL/Perk system in dialogue with any meaningful game impact.  It was noted and included in some DLC but the damage was done.
Voice work for the protagonist is IMHO, decent, especially the female lead.  Followers and other voice work is also pretty well done.
Speaking of followers, one of the things I most enjoy about F4 is some of the interaction with these characters.  I wish they had gone a bit further but what is here is enjoyable.  Follower AI is not smart period, and pathing is at times an issue.
The world is incredibly well done (not mind blowing graphics wise but solidly well done) and the atmosphere, again IMHO, is some of the best.  In fact I would go so far as to say it truly does feel alive.  Settlements lend a feeling of progress to civilization and some of the coolest mods out there really capture the essence and show off just how good an element this part of the game is....BUT....its not everyones cup of tea.  If you like this kind of thing youtube it first to get an idea of how it works.
If you are into exploration, this game has that in spades.  Every nook and cranny seems packed with something to find, be it a story, or loot, eye candy, or "Danger Will Robinson, Danger!!"  Some of the quests are very well done and really add flavor to locations.  Some critics have dinged the quest system as repetetive in nature, especially the settlement ones.  Most of this is easily avoidable or rejectable.  Part of the criticism is deserved, but overly harsh.  I would just say that there is some really great stuff for the taking here, and part of the brilliance of F4 is that the vast, and I mean vast majority of it is up to you to complete, or not.
Speaking of quests, the main story line has its critics as well.  This is an incredibly subjective thing of course so your mileage will vary.  I personally enjoyed most of it.  Parts were "meh", parts were great, and certain parts I really loved.  I never once thought it was terrible.  Having said that, I can understand those that felt otherwise.  But like any short story, you will find people who hate it.  Now, if you are here for the story...well....this may not be the game for you, MAY not be.  It really depends what you like and how the hell am I supposed to know what you like.
The real beauty of F4 comes with the modding community.  Quite frankly with the right mods this game just is freaking fun.  Plain and simple, critics be damned.  There is a mod or two or twenty out there for you, and if you do your homework, and like this type of game, you cannot go wrong.  There is just so much here to offer.
Now this is just one mans humble opinion regarding recent activity, but...I highly suggest you do some youtubbing and tune out the CC critics for now, the tin foil hats are out in droves.  Arguing with them is pointless, apparently Bethesda has given up on the community, made a pact with the devil to consume modder souls, and is currently in talks with Amazon to take over the world and force people to drink the coolaid.   I highly suggest you just judge the game for itself and let the modder community decide for itself if it wants to participate.  Time will tell if the Creation Club works, or doesn't, and Bethesda will reap the reward or pay the price.
Just as it should be.

Very unique and generally outstanding game; though not for the faint of heart. It's soul-crushingly brutal, at times it makes you want to just quit and never come back, though the promise of riches and glory is hard to pass up.
The atmosphere is amazing for a side-scroller, absolutely incredible voice acting from the narrator. The music while in my opinion less impressive than the narrator's voice acting, still adds a very fitting touch of dreary hopelessness and despair; the ambience, though subtle, also reinforces that.
In terms of gameplay, it's fairly standard by way of RPGs, kill monsters, collect items, upgrade your characters; however as you probably already know there is a significant emphasis on managing the mental health of your heroes, in addition the traditional system of physical health. It is in part this system that adds an additional layer of brutal difficulty to the game.
Especially when starting out, you'll be wanting to upgrade a lot of different things; the problem however is that resources and gold are scarce, so you'll have to think carefully about where you get the most bang for your buck. This ties in very well with preserving the mental health of your heroes. If you spend resources to alleviate one hero of his problems, another hero, or even multiple heroes will have to forego certain upgrades or medical treatment. The game often forces you to throw certain heroes under the bus, and then blames you for their fate, which simply further adds to the atmosphere and difficulty, both of which is exactly what the game is about.
If you're looking for a brutal RPG gaming experience that isn't Dark Souls, I would definitely recommend you try out Darkest Dungeon.
On a final note, there are many many many critics of this game, some are completely insane (obviously they cracked under the pressure of the Darkest Dungeon) and some have fair enough points. That said, many of those critics, criticize the game for it's difficulty, either directly, or in some cases indirectly, but just because they prefer their gaming experiences on a silver platter, doesn't necessarily mean everyone else does, even if they can't fathom that. My point is, do watch out for some of the negative reviews, or at least think about what they're CLAIMING an extra time, especially some of the older ones.

Alright, well, let's start with the game being hard as hell, to the point where it's masochistic. I bought this game on sale and from what I had seen I was sold straightaway. the art design in this game is fantastic not to mention the sound gives you a feel of hopelessness  inside each hero especially when you're camping and you've only cleared 40% of the rooms and your healer is insane. They hit this feeling well and I applaud them immensely. The game is fycking depressing man.
But...
They might as well call this game  "Dodge: the game. You've never seen such a luck based game like this."
The game punishes you no matter how smart you play and preparing before a run has a somewhat little effect on the run its self. A lot of the mechanics are percentage based so a battle can work in your favor or go against you entirely, everything from critical hits to poison chance to bleed to dodge to deathblow resist and so on and so forth. So if Johnny scumsh!t on the enemy team has a 50% to resist your blight(poison) attack then you can miss him entirely or hit him every time, there's no skill here you're better off praying to jebus than being smart, outmanuvering your opponents or when sh!t hits the fan, being able to adapt and roll with the punches. I get that this is a rouge-like and randomness is supposed to be much more of a feature but when you lose a level 6 hellion with very rare trinkets and you've pumped 50k of gold into making her a powerhouse goddess to a swine god (boss) because your occultist kept healing her for 0-4 HP the entire run, and healing crits are nowhere to be seen. Then youve really got to question if this is really fair. The devs saying "darkest dungeon is supposed to be hard, idiot lol XD" feels more like a cop out for not balancing the game. A blend of roguelike RPG, Xcom style squad and base management and a very important stress mechanic, with Cthulhuverse monstrosities that drain the very sanity of adventurers, this indie title has proven explosively popular since it's first release. Rightly so, in my opinion.
The community has since divided itself, becoming impossible to please. Every change has quite vocal detractors as a result. Many of these simply disagree with their favorite strategy getting nerfed. That said, the old "release something OP, nerf later" method of releasing new content is in full swing.
Don't let any of this confuse you, this is one of the best games to come out in recent years. It's pleasingly difficult and complex, the sound and artwork is superb and the narrator's haunting voice is magnificent.
Pro's:
- Deep and varied gameplay
- Immersive atmosphere, looks great
- Unique combination of mechanics, one of it's kind
Con's
- Updates may result in a sudden difficulty spike or a favorite strategy becoming unviable
Verdict: Good game, highly recommended.

I Can't reccommend this for anyone except die hard Xcom fans desperate for more xcom action. If you're interested in Xcom and havent played the originals, and the reboot, AND long war, don't buy. They bumbled this one.
The bad:
- Baffling gameplay design choices
- A huge system hog for seemingly simple graphics
- A crappy interface, especially for PC (worse than the last xcom!)
The good:
- Combat is still very satisfying. But way more bullet spongey
I don't understand the direction they are taking this series. It truely baffles and confuses me. The last game stripped xcom of all of its deepest (some may say complicated) elements, like soldier stats (which made them individually unique), action points, etc. This one continues to remove the things we love, like the (granted, dumbed down) UFO interception system, but on top of that ADDS a ridiculously convoluted geoscape and base system. What the hell were they THINKING?
There are 400 differnt resources. Its like an Iphone game where you get wood and ore and gold, but you gotta pay 5 dollars for the super special pink crystals! Unless of course you want to wait around with your thumb up your♥♥♥♥♥for 48 hours.
You run around the map playing a persistant game of wack a mole. But there is always an obvious choice. There is no STRATEGY in this strategy game.
You get to maticulesly place every scientist and engineer, assigning them to various tasks. Cuz why not add some needless, unfullfilling micromanagement to the game?!
You're never really sure what youre acomplishing and why! I need some intel for this, then gotta reseach that, then make contect with this guy then fly over here and pat my head and rub my belly and WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥! How could you make this such a convoluted MESS, yet still say, "Players are too stupid for action points! Thats too complicated! No more interceptors, its too involved! It needs to be accessable!" Are you KIDDING me?!
Besides the gameplay choices being incomprehensible, I'd like to adress the graphics and interface. Can we please stop with this trend of making everything smaller and smaller, and calling that "graphical improvement?!" Please! The buttons in this game are 2x2 pixels. You need a microscope AND a gyroscope to read the text. Because not only is it impossibly small, they thought it would be a silly goof to add a scrambling effect every 3 seconds while you're trying to read 4 paragraphs of text for every research project!
You can only rotate the map in 90 degree incriments instead of 45 now. Which makes it enranging when you're tring to click the single pixel that lets you move to the spot behind cover instead of the one where your genitals are perfectly lined up with the aliens gun barrel.
WHY can I play fallout 4 without issue and this game drops to 3 FPS on the lowest settings? The graphics look like 2006's Sam and Max, so why does this game require a monster PC?
Speaking of which, the graphical design of this game (and to a lesser extent, the previous one) is lame. Its designed for children. I feel like a dork when I play, because I'm looking at guys with cartoonishly large guns and guile haircuts run around in Anime armor. If thats your thing, thats cool. One day you'll be a grown up too and feel some shame!
All that being said, it feels a lot like the last game, and the combat is satisfying. However, they really upped the bullet spongeyness of enimies and added more needless, pointless, convoluted elements to combat as well, in the form of hacking. Which is COMPLETELY RNG. Thats fun too right? Thats what people love about strategy games. The RNG....
So get it if you've exhasted the previous games. Do not support this kind of decision making otherwise.

Did you enjoy Enemy Unknown? Or Enemy Within?
Then you'll more than likely be pretty disappointed by this release. Now before the fans start shouting words of hatred towards this review.. I will say, this isn't a bad game at all. Infact.. it's much more challenging and I would even go as far as saying, it's far better in almost everyway from the previous game. So why the Negative review?
Turn times.. 90% of your missions now have god damn turn times. There's no taking your time setting up ambushes.. no taking your time making sure your squad can overwatch retreating targets.. You have to rush rush rush. For a start you're given no indication of how many enemies are on the map.. just 8 turns remaining, and a whole heap of terrain to cover. It's not tactical combat because we're not given the opportunity to be tactical. Most of my Excellent games have been by the skin of my teeth and pure bloody luck! But it doesn't stop there.. because you'll also have a countdown on your main map as well.. indicating how long before the world is destroyed by the Aliens.
My biggest gripe with the game though is the path finding. In the previous games you could hide behind a wall as long as it wasnt the edge of the wall. This meant you couldn't shoot the enemy, but they couldn't shoot you either without some sort of explosive being used. Not anymore... Enemy's can pull you through a wall, shoot you through a wall, see you through a wall... infact, im not even sure why there are walls :S. Once concealment is gone, every troop on the map is visible no matter if he/she is hiding in a building.. at the back of the map.. sitting in a dustbin... wearing a penguin suit..
So it's not a bad game.. it has allot of potential. It's far far more challenging than EW. It's just lost its appeal for me. I like the tactical, stratagy side of the combat... it's just not fun anymore. That being said I will more than likely complete the game, I just wont be playing it over again and again like I did EW.

Overall a pretty solid game, with several immense caveats.
Some people seem to buy into this idea that blind, unbalanced challenge is 'fun.' Some don't. There's a fine line in there and where exactly that line should lie is going to vary from one individual to the next.
Frankly, the game is balaned to intentionally be badly balanced. There are some options to tune it one way or the other, so thankfully they've avoided totally shooting themselves in the proverbial feet with this feature, and thus it's not a total no-go for someone who just wants to enjoy a challenging, but not ridiculous, game.
The biggest issue is the vast number of things that are totally out of your control - roguelikes and challenge are fun, pure-RNG losses are not. And there's a lot of that here. Furthermore, many of the dungeon encounterables are depressingly shallow. They usually are 100% good if use item, or guaranteed bad/nothing otherwise. As soon as you figure that out, the "oh man, do I open this? Do I touch that? Do I examine this box?" all goes out the window. They should have put more variety into the encounterable dungeon objects. Basically you'll sometimes find, say, a box. Except the box is trapped 80% of the time without a kay, 20% you get something, and with a key it's always loot. There's no real  uncertainty there, it's obviously best to skip it without a key.
The character classes, art style, and aesthetic are pretty solid - and the whole 'feel' is very well executed! The issue class-wise is that, frankly, a bunch of them just kinda suck compared to others. A few of the classes are undeniable powerhouses and are nearly required to succeed, whereas others are neat or interesting, but flop hard. For people who enjoy stranger classes this is a big let down because, as above, the intentionally unfair balancing. You can't really afford to screw around or have fun, you pretty much are expected if not forced to min-max it up.
But again, the randomness.. It's an integral part of roguelikes and their ilk, but it has to be done well. I really don't think this game did it well, and again I understand it's under the guise of "punishing" and "hardcore" and all that, but that's just a recent trend and excuse for "lazy development." It's easy to make a stupidly hard game, it's hard to make a reasonably challenging one.
With all that said, though, it is a pretty interesting and fun game. Once you get the gist and feel of it, though, it turns into an endless and repetitious grind to work your way through various areas.
For $20, much less $25, I can't recommend it. There's only four or five dungeons, and by "dungeons" I mean art tilesets that are randomly arranged. And I give them kudos for their art and aesthetic achievement, and the cool variety of classes, but the latter is poorly balanced in terms of usefulness and several feel nearly unplayable or pointless to attempt to use in comparison with others. And I'm not talking they have some useful 'niche', they just don't. :(
I'd merrily recommend the game in the $15 price range just because, again, it ultimately boils down to dungeon grinding and RNG luck, there's really not more depth than that. You can carefully build your party and equip items and such all you want, and you'll just grind through the same dungeons against the same monsters, and then get unlucky and lose your best two characters to a few bad rounds of combat, or they'll run out of town for several weeks for some random uncontrollable reason, etc.
It really is decent, it's pretty good and reasonably solid, but not for the price point. It just doesn't have the depth and play time - it's fun for several hours in several stretches, but it gets stale fast once you get your feet solidly planted and get a grasp on things, unless you severely dig repetitious grinding with intentionally poor balance.

How do you review a series you enjoyed through many installments and through two different platforms? I will be reviewing dark souls 3 in a pro/ con style and end with my final conclusions.
Pro:
Nice scenery. The game looks amazing with the better graphics overhal compaired to previous installments. Besides that every location you go to looks nice and unique, easy to tell the difference between one location compaired to another. To add to that the different worlds are filled with enemies that feel cohesive to their respective land.
The music is great. I enjoy the music that is played at the fire link shrine and also the boss music for the abyss watchers.
Plenty of weapons to use. There are many of weapons from your basic solo weapons like swords, maces, ect. Now they add in the feature to have dual weapons. So the player must equip it to whatever hand they wish and they will use a single weapon but if they two hand it...the character will have 2 of that weapon. It is cool and can provide some neat combat moves.
Con:
The reuse of old enemies. It is less like they tried to add new things but made the game based on things fans liked from old dark souls games. Really it is pretty lazy and i did not want to see the wheel skeleton enemies or multiple variations of the first boss in dark souls 1.
The lack of choice in dark souls since dark souls 2. What dark souls 2 easy? yes but it had choice to it. It allowed the player to experience the game on an easier level while if players challenge themselves they could do that with their own choice. None of that is here in this game which really sucks.
The enemy placement is pretty bad which messes up flow even for this game. The idea of putting tank like enemies on narrow platforms is a horrible idea. I dont mind challenge but what this is....it is not a challenge rather poor level design.
Dark souls 3 takes inspiration from old dark souls and bloodborn. That is cool but the issue is that dark souls isnt bloodborn. Bloodborn is a fast pace dark souls game that has its mechanics dealing around being agressive and quick dodging and such. Dark souls is not that. What dark souls is...is slower and more thoughtful as to when to strike and when to dodge roll. The bosses in the two series are different and combining them in this game is a beautiful mess. It provides a clash between mechanics and combat.
There is a swamp level that not only does it poison the player similar to lower blight town from dark souls but it is unbarebly slow.  Sure there is a way to speed it up but why is it even here? It feels like a checklist in all souls and souls like games.
Conclusion:
In short i am a major dark souls fan. Played all the souls games except bloodborn on multiple different platforms till I 100% it but this game is tied for the most unenjoyable souls experience with dark souls 1 and salt and sanctuary. It is  not that i am a casual because that is obviously false but it deals with how enemies are really agressive like playing bloodborn but clashing with the slower pace of dark souls. Could i reccommend the game...no. Sure the game looks better and the music is nice but the issues are a big problem.

I Can't reccommend this for anyone except die hard Xcom fans desperate for more xcom action. If you're interested in Xcom and havent played the originals, and the reboot, AND long war, don't buy. They bumbled this one.
The bad:
- Baffling gameplay design choices
- A huge system hog for seemingly simple graphics
- A crappy interface, especially for PC (worse than the last xcom!)
The good:
- Combat is still very satisfying. But way more bullet spongey
I don't understand the direction they are taking this series. It truely baffles and confuses me. The last game stripped xcom of all of its deepest (some may say complicated) elements, like soldier stats (which made them individually unique), action points, etc. This one continues to remove the things we love, like the (granted, dumbed down) UFO interception system, but on top of that ADDS a ridiculously convoluted geoscape and base system. What the hell were they THINKING?
There are 400 differnt resources. Its like an Iphone game where you get wood and ore and gold, but you gotta pay 5 dollars for the super special pink crystals! Unless of course you want to wait around with your thumb up your♥♥♥♥♥for 48 hours.
You run around the map playing a persistant game of wack a mole. But there is always an obvious choice. There is no STRATEGY in this strategy game.
You get to maticulesly place every scientist and engineer, assigning them to various tasks. Cuz why not add some needless, unfullfilling micromanagement to the game?!
You're never really sure what youre acomplishing and why! I need some intel for this, then gotta reseach that, then make contect with this guy then fly over here and pat my head and rub my belly and WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥! How could you make this such a convoluted MESS, yet still say, "Players are too stupid for action points! Thats too complicated! No more interceptors, its too involved! It needs to be accessable!" Are you KIDDING me?!
Besides the gameplay choices being incomprehensible, I'd like to adress the graphics and interface. Can we please stop with this trend of making everything smaller and smaller, and calling that "graphical improvement?!" Please! The buttons in this game are 2x2 pixels. You need a microscope AND a gyroscope to read the text. Because not only is it impossibly small, they thought it would be a silly goof to add a scrambling effect every 3 seconds while you're trying to read 4 paragraphs of text for every research project!
You can only rotate the map in 90 degree incriments instead of 45 now. Which makes it enranging when you're tring to click the single pixel that lets you move to the spot behind cover instead of the one where your genitals are perfectly lined up with the aliens gun barrel.
WHY can I play fallout 4 without issue and this game drops to 3 FPS on the lowest settings? The graphics look like 2006's Sam and Max, so why does this game require a monster PC?
Speaking of which, the graphical design of this game (and to a lesser extent, the previous one) is lame. Its designed for children. I feel like a dork when I play, because I'm looking at guys with cartoonishly large guns and guile haircuts run around in Anime armor. If thats your thing, thats cool. One day you'll be a grown up too and feel some shame!
All that being said, it feels a lot like the last game, and the combat is satisfying. However, they really upped the bullet spongeyness of enimies and added more needless, pointless, convoluted elements to combat as well, in the form of hacking. Which is COMPLETELY RNG. Thats fun too right? Thats what people love about strategy games. The RNG....
So get it if you've exhasted the previous games. Do not support this kind of decision making otherwise.

Without doubts the worst in the series, it isn't a bad game, mind you, but it does mean that I can't recommend it.
I have much love for some parts of the pve experience, but due to a couple changes to the core mechanics (poise, stamina costs, infusions) the game just falls flat compared to the others in the series. It's like Fromsoftware took the worst out of both bloodborne and ds1, and mixed it together into this game. However I'd still recommend this if this is your first from the Dark Souls series, since it is the easiest to get into of all of them. But if you've played Dark souls 1 and 2, prepare to be disappointed.
The good:
-The "story" mode feels good to play through, DLC is good albeit a bit overpriced for the content you receive (mainly looking at ariandel here)
-Cool bosses
-Combat is unbelievably smooth
-As usual, the games in the souls series have immense replayability
-Lots of armor/weapons to pick and play with
The bad:
-Enemies never seem to run out of stamina
-Weapon balance is terrible in PvP, there's a couple weapons which you will encounter every other fight
-Phantom hits in online play
-Shields are pretty much useless in PvE/PvP
-All areas are made out of either a brown or grey colour, which gets tiring rather quick
-Poise mechanic is executed poorly
-It barely matters whether you equip heavy or light armor.
-The newly introduced Weapon Arts, while cool, lead to an incredibly stale pvp-experience where you will encounter the same kind of repeated weapon art combo every time.
-Weapon arts are pretty much useless in most of the PvE content compared to regular attacks
Having said all this, I'd give Dark Souls 3 (Including DLC)  a solid 6/10
It's a worthwhile game to pick up if you're fresh to the souls series, but as a fan of the souls-series, I can't recommend it.

I would recomend this game bottom line, i have 885 hours and climbing for god sakes, but lets go over some of the pros and cons really quick, ill be giving a TL:DR to start and then explaining why i think that way. This is a review just on the game its self
Good Gunplay
Good replayablity
Well balanced stats and different playstyles with the new perk system
a large map to explore
Multipul sides to take
The Crafting/Settlement building
The number of companions
There isnt alot of "Vendor Trash"
lots of side quests/Random Events
Quality of Life improvements
Cons
Some of the dialog options are a bit forced
Some things arent as flushed out as they could be
The story can fall flat for some people
Not a ton of different armor sets
OP things like power armor are too readily avaliable
Thats the TL;DR
Now lets dive into it shall we, starting with the Cons here, some of the dialog is a bit forced, making you go down paths you dont really want to go down, such as talking with Preston in concord, there really isnt so much of a go ♥♥♥♥ yourself option as it were. There are also times, where some of the things you say arent really what you want to say, and the little dialog options can be a bit vague, which can be a issue if your trying to max rep with a companion or you want to say very specific things.
Some things simply arent as flushed out as they could be, there are issues here or there, some of the characters could have a bit more substance for example, like the guard at the front of dimond city, who i really want to know the story of and what happens to but i cant, but for a game this massive frankly its to be expected, there is alot happening and its hard to get all the little guys.
Im not going to spoil the game, but in short the end story can feel a bit forced, or unintresting to some people. I personally enjoyed it the first time round with each faction and then started to veer off to the more exciting adventuring and side quests. ((i also was dispointed in some parts so i started coming up with conspircy theroies about the story which i find great joy in.))
There are very few armor sets in the game ((without mods)) even fewer if we are only counting armor that is worth a damn, which is a bit of a shame, and the armor customization is a bit meh. It can kinda kill the flow of gear when it comes to armor, but if your into the upgrading armor part of the game you can always go to power armor, or go my route which was to just play in first person and stop giving a damn.
Power is to OP and readily avalible you get a complete set in 2 quests, and its really really broken, and the power cores frankly arent rare enough, so it gives the player an insane advantage, in other fallout games you really had to work really really hard at it but in Fallout 4 they just offer it to you. Personally i refuse to wear it, and that easily fixes that issue, or give myself a level cap of 40-50 before i can use it! :)
Overall for the Cons alot of them can be easily avoided if you choose to do so, but i suggest you try it for yourself and come to your own conclusions and solutions.
And now to the Pros! The gun play is better then any other fallout game lets just end it there, the gun customization feels fun and rewarding, especially for the more advanced weapons, and it feels very smooth, and the fact the cross hairs and iron sights/scopes are actually useful are a god sent for players like me who refuse to use V.A.T.S. ((i dont use VATS because frankly i feel as though it is completely skilless, basiclly a free aim bot, but thats a personal thought.))
Lets talk about Replayablity the game has it in spades, its far superior to most fallout games in that respect, the leveling system helps with it quite alot, there are quite a few paths to do if you so choose, more locations then you can count, settlements to build, side missions to do, gain maximum affliation with all the companions, fun gun play, and so on. All of which results in a game that you can play for a long time over and over.
The Perks/Stats opposed to other games i like how it doesnt force you to pick in the start and stay that way, and the new perk system really gives the options for unique and fun builds, my personal favorites, are explosive, juggernuat, and stealth like builds, and there are many different combos, a great thing about it, is by doing a certain build you dont feel massively overpowered, and most Perks feel satisfying and useful, except a few that miss the mark a little.
The Map is big and there is alot of fun exciting places to explore, and figure out what happened pre/post war there. This one is pretty easy to explain, that being sad this game isnt the most friendly to players who want to be more sniper like, as alot of gameplay happens in close couters but it can be done! :)
You can pick from 4 different factions with different morals, goals, and side quests, characters, and storylines! that being said you must complete a minimum 4-5 main storyline quests before one of the factions becomes avaliable and your really able to pick which side you want to join. For me though those 4-5 quests are good because it gives me time to deside who my character is and where they should go.
Crafting and settlements are a huge change and frankly they give alot of life to some builds and are really fun to play around with. the crafting system is really something awesome and building a custom heat seaking quad rocket luacher frankly feels suppppper badass. The settlements are also a ton of fun i personally enjoyed making a settlement empire on a few characters and building defenses, though sometimes the snapping feature can be a tad buggy ((and some other settlement things)) which is a disapointment and something i can easily overlook.
There are alot of companions all with different storylines, perks, likes and dislikes ((i think there is 13? someone correct me if im incorrect.)) This makes the game alot of fun especially when they have comments to bring to the conversation or talking about a zone or action, it makes the game feel more realistic, and enjoyable! :D
There isnt much vendor trash, almost everything can be used in one way or another, so you will rarely be turning down even the simple things, such as desk fans for those bolts, or duct tape for the adheasive. I find this enjoyable as going to the vendor for an hour and a half to sell out my 300 pounds of garbage makes for really unsatisfying gameplay.
There are alot of Sidequests and random events to keep you intrested for quite sometime, and alot of these quests you will find as you just randomly stroll through the wastleland, which will send you to new exciting places, and give things purpose, other then to just shoot things and get awesome loot ((which i personally adore!)), Not the mention the Magazines and bobble heads that are fun to collect. The random events also give the game dynamic things which can be quite refreshing.
There are alot of quality of life changes as well, such as facial reconstruction if you messed up in character creation, or you can get tattoos or get unique hairstyles, the ability to be able to add to your S.P.E.C.I.A.L Stats and other things like that, as well as the new store junk button, which makes life just that much more enjoyable.
Does it have issues yes? is it a great game? Hell Yes! do i suggest you buy it? Yuppers! :D i hope this helped you :)

Did you enjoy Enemy Unknown? Or Enemy Within?
Then you'll more than likely be pretty disappointed by this release. Now before the fans start shouting words of hatred towards this review.. I will say, this isn't a bad game at all. Infact.. it's much more challenging and I would even go as far as saying, it's far better in almost everyway from the previous game. So why the Negative review?
Turn times.. 90% of your missions now have god damn turn times. There's no taking your time setting up ambushes.. no taking your time making sure your squad can overwatch retreating targets.. You have to rush rush rush. For a start you're given no indication of how many enemies are on the map.. just 8 turns remaining, and a whole heap of terrain to cover. It's not tactical combat because we're not given the opportunity to be tactical. Most of my Excellent games have been by the skin of my teeth and pure bloody luck! But it doesn't stop there.. because you'll also have a countdown on your main map as well.. indicating how long before the world is destroyed by the Aliens.
My biggest gripe with the game though is the path finding. In the previous games you could hide behind a wall as long as it wasnt the edge of the wall. This meant you couldn't shoot the enemy, but they couldn't shoot you either without some sort of explosive being used. Not anymore... Enemy's can pull you through a wall, shoot you through a wall, see you through a wall... infact, im not even sure why there are walls :S. Once concealment is gone, every troop on the map is visible no matter if he/she is hiding in a building.. at the back of the map.. sitting in a dustbin... wearing a penguin suit..
So it's not a bad game.. it has allot of potential. It's far far more challenging than EW. It's just lost its appeal for me. I like the tactical, stratagy side of the combat... it's just not fun anymore. That being said I will more than likely complete the game, I just wont be playing it over again and again like I did EW.

Trove is a great little MMO Trove is a some-what sandbox/dungeon crawler game that does not have any kind of story but encourages exploration. Trove let's you build your own home/base with a ton of options. You can explore dungeons, go on mini raids, sail on the ocean and fight pirates, fly, and much more. It is a free game with an in game store, but nothing in there utterly breaks the game experience. The store has some cosmetics with the same stats as anything in the game. There is a nice selection of classes in Trove with more being added fairly often that shake up the playing experince. Each class has it's own skills and more are unlocked as you level that class up. The classes can be swapped, so if you don't like the feel of a certain class you can always swap. The combat system is simple but smooth and fun. There is something for the more casual players in this game of making a nice home, and having some fun exploring with friends, along with rare mounts to craft/collect. A very funny game to play with some friends.

While I love the game and think that it's great, I can no excuse some of the issues that currently plague it. I will revise this review when/if the issues are resolved.
Pros:
- AI is significantly smarter than in EU.
- New mechanics/classes/buildings/tech/etc serve to spice things up while keeping true to the base game.
- The tutorial is pretty hand-holdy, but it does a good job of explaining the new and old mechanics.
Cons:
- The game has a fair amounts of bugs (possibly only visual?) when it comes to the ability to fire or move through walls and floors. I've had units that were panicked drop through a seemingly solid floor to go attack an enemy. I've been attacked through a seemingly solid wall where the enemy should not have had line of sight.
- It does not utilize SLI very much (if at all).
- Performance is pretty bad and I haven't seen it pull above 30 fps on max settings, even though my computer is more than capable of it.
- There are some strange things going on with the audio settings. My settings are ignored in the unskippable intro screens and during cinematics, so my ears end up getting blasted.
Currently, due to these issues, I am unfortuantely not able to recommend it to people. I am sure that these issues will be resolved shortly, but due to recent events, I won't trust it until I see it.

Trove is a great little MMO Trove is a some-what sandbox/dungeon crawler game that does not have any kind of story but encourages exploration. Trove let's you build your own home/base with a ton of options. You can explore dungeons, go on mini raids, sail on the ocean and fight pirates, fly, and much more. There is something for the more casual players in this game of making a nice home, and having some fun exploring with friends, along with rare mounts to craft/collect. A very funny game to play with some friends.

Without doubts the worst in the series, it isn't a bad game, mind you, but it does mean that I can't recommend it.
I have much love for some parts of the pve experience, but due to a couple changes to the core mechanics (poise, stamina costs, infusions) the game just falls flat compared to the others in the series. It's like Fromsoftware took the worst out of both bloodborne and ds1, and mixed it together into this game. However I'd still recommend this if this is your first from the Dark Souls series, since it is the easiest to get into of all of them. But if you've played Dark souls 1 and 2, prepare to be disappointed.
The good:
-The "story" mode feels good to play through, DLC is good albeit a bit overpriced for the content you receive (mainly looking at ariandel here)
-Cool bosses
-Combat is unbelievably smooth
-As usual, the games in the souls series have immense replayability
-Lots of armor/weapons to pick and play with
The bad:
-Enemies never seem to run out of stamina
-Weapon balance is terrible in PvP, there's a couple weapons which you will encounter every other fight
-Phantom hits in online play
-Shields are pretty much useless in PvE/PvP
-All areas are made out of either a brown or grey colour, which gets tiring rather quick
-Poise mechanic is executed poorly
-It barely matters whether you equip heavy or light armor.
-The newly introduced Weapon Arts, while cool, lead to an incredibly stale pvp-experience where you will encounter the same kind of repeated weapon art combo every time.
-Weapon arts are pretty much useless in most of the PvE content compared to regular attacks
Having said all this, I'd give Dark Souls 3 (Including DLC)  a solid 6/10
It's a worthwhile game to pick up if you're fresh to the souls series, but as a fan of the souls-series, I can't recommend it.

I would recomend this game bottom line, i have 885 hours and climbing for god sakes, but lets go over some of the pros and cons really quick, ill be giving a TL:DR to start and then explaining why i think that way. This is a review just on the game its self
Good Gunplay
Good replayablity
Well balanced stats and different playstyles with the new perk system
a large map to explore
Multipul sides to take
The Crafting/Settlement building
The number of companions
There isnt alot of "Vendor Trash"
lots of side quests/Random Events
Quality of Life improvements
Cons
Some of the dialog options are a bit forced
Some things arent as flushed out as they could be
The story can fall flat for some people
Not a ton of different armor sets
OP things like power armor are too readily avaliable
Thats the TL;DR
Now lets dive into it shall we, starting with the Cons here, some of the dialog is a bit forced, making you go down paths you dont really want to go down, such as talking with Preston in concord, there really isnt so much of a go ♥♥♥♥ yourself option as it were. There are also times, where some of the things you say arent really what you want to say, and the little dialog options can be a bit vague, which can be a issue if your trying to max rep with a companion or you want to say very specific things.
Some things simply arent as flushed out as they could be, there are issues here or there, some of the characters could have a bit more substance for example, like the guard at the front of dimond city, who i really want to know the story of and what happens to but i cant, but for a game this massive frankly its to be expected, there is alot happening and its hard to get all the little guys.
Im not going to spoil the game, but in short the end story can feel a bit forced, or unintresting to some people. I personally enjoyed it the first time round with each faction and then started to veer off to the more exciting adventuring and side quests. ((i also was dispointed in some parts so i started coming up with conspircy theroies about the story which i find great joy in.))
There are very few armor sets in the game ((without mods)) even fewer if we are only counting armor that is worth a damn, which is a bit of a shame, and the armor customization is a bit meh. It can kinda kill the flow of gear when it comes to armor, but if your into the upgrading armor part of the game you can always go to power armor, or go my route which was to just play in first person and stop giving a damn.
Power is to OP and readily avalible you get a complete set in 2 quests, and its really really broken, and the power cores frankly arent rare enough, so it gives the player an insane advantage, in other fallout games you really had to work really really hard at it but in Fallout 4 they just offer it to you. Personally i refuse to wear it, and that easily fixes that issue, or give myself a level cap of 40-50 before i can use it! :)
Overall for the Cons alot of them can be easily avoided if you choose to do so, but i suggest you try it for yourself and come to your own conclusions and solutions.
And now to the Pros! The gun play is better then any other fallout game lets just end it there, the gun customization feels fun and rewarding, especially for the more advanced weapons, and it feels very smooth, and the fact the cross hairs and iron sights/scopes are actually useful are a god sent for players like me who refuse to use V.A.T.S. ((i dont use VATS because frankly i feel as though it is completely skilless, basiclly a free aim bot, but thats a personal thought.))
Lets talk about Replayablity the game has it in spades, its far superior to most fallout games in that respect, the leveling system helps with it quite alot, there are quite a few paths to do if you so choose, more locations then you can count, settlements to build, side missions to do, gain maximum affliation with all the companions, fun gun play, and so on. All of which results in a game that you can play for a long time over and over.
The Perks/Stats opposed to other games i like how it doesnt force you to pick in the start and stay that way, and the new perk system really gives the options for unique and fun builds, my personal favorites, are explosive, juggernuat, and stealth like builds, and there are many different combos, a great thing about it, is by doing a certain build you dont feel massively overpowered, and most Perks feel satisfying and useful, except a few that miss the mark a little.
The Map is big and there is alot of fun exciting places to explore, and figure out what happened pre/post war there. This one is pretty easy to explain, that being sad this game isnt the most friendly to players who want to be more sniper like, as alot of gameplay happens in close couters but it can be done! :)
You can pick from 4 different factions with different morals, goals, and side quests, characters, and storylines! that being said you must complete a minimum 4-5 main storyline quests before one of the factions becomes avaliable and your really able to pick which side you want to join. For me though those 4-5 quests are good because it gives me time to deside who my character is and where they should go.
Crafting and settlements are a huge change and frankly they give alot of life to some builds and are really fun to play around with. the crafting system is really something awesome and building a custom heat seaking quad rocket luacher frankly feels suppppper badass. The settlements are also a ton of fun i personally enjoyed making a settlement empire on a few characters and building defenses, though sometimes the snapping feature can be a tad buggy ((and some other settlement things)) which is a disapointment and something i can easily overlook.
There are alot of companions all with different storylines, perks, likes and dislikes ((i think there is 13? someone correct me if im incorrect.)) This makes the game alot of fun especially when they have comments to bring to the conversation or talking about a zone or action, it makes the game feel more realistic, and enjoyable! :D
There isnt much vendor trash, almost everything can be used in one way or another, so you will rarely be turning down even the simple things, such as desk fans for those bolts, or duct tape for the adheasive. I find this enjoyable as going to the vendor for an hour and a half to sell out my 300 pounds of garbage makes for really unsatisfying gameplay.
There are alot of Sidequests and random events to keep you intrested for quite sometime, and alot of these quests you will find as you just randomly stroll through the wastleland, which will send you to new exciting places, and give things purpose, other then to just shoot things and get awesome loot ((which i personally adore!)), Not the mention the Magazines and bobble heads that are fun to collect. The random events also give the game dynamic things which can be quite refreshing.
There are alot of quality of life changes as well, such as facial reconstruction if you messed up in character creation, or you can get tattoos or get unique hairstyles, the ability to be able to add to your S.P.E.C.I.A.L Stats and other things like that, as well as the new store junk button, which makes life just that much more enjoyable.
Does it have issues yes? is it a great game? Hell Yes! do i suggest you buy it? Yuppers! :D i hope this helped you :)

You know what this review's going to say. Fallout 4 is garbage. It's quite possibly the worst game Bethesda's made. That's how I see it, anyway. I originally bought this game on console, back when I USED to be a console gamer. But I had a chance at a free weekend where I thought "Yeah, the game sucked, but I can probably salvage it with mods, like I do with every game on PC." Long story short, not even mods improved what's ultimately just a bland experience. Although I haven't tried Frost. Frost looks like a great mod. It completely overhauls the game. But I digress..
The shooting is okay. There's really nothing wrong with the shooting. If you're buying this game expecting a shooter set in the Fallout universe, you're going to have a blast like I did..For a few days, anyway. If you're expecting a Fallout game, you'll be disappointed.  Having a voiced protagonist really takes away from the RPG aspect. The character you'll spend hours customizing in the AMAZING customization menu is not your own character. It is not your own story. Go ahead and invest most of your points into charisma. It won't make any significant differences in a game where violence IS the only answer, and the only way to move forward.
Let's see..What else? Graphics are terrible. It really is an ugly looking game. I'd strongly advise you to use ENBs or reshades..Anything you can get your hands on. It won't change the games hideous engine, but it'll help. Settlements. Settlements are an afterthought. Thanks to mods, you can really improve on settlement building, though. Even the dumbass settlers who are no smarter than Fawks from Fallout 3.
Now, I know what you're thinking "Oh, if he references Fallout 3 a lot, he must be blinded by nostalgia. Those games weren't great." True, but from Fallout 1 onwards to Vegas, Fallouts always had indepth RPG elements. You could go through the game as a pacifist, bringing peace to the wasteland that doesn't involve ramboing against a bunch of helpless raiders.
Fallout 4: It's Actually Kinda Okay With Mods Edition.

Without doubts the worst in the series, it isn't a bad game, mind you, but it does mean that I can't recommend it.
I have much love for some parts of the pve experience, but due to a couple changes to the core mechanics (poise, stamina costs, infusions) the game just falls flat compared to the others in the series. It's like Fromsoftware took the worst out of both bloodborne and ds1, and mixed it together into this game. However I'd still recommend this if this is your first from the Dark Souls series, since it is the easiest to get into of all of them. But if you've played Dark souls 1 and 2, prepare to be disappointed.
The good:
-The "story" mode feels good to play through, DLC is good albeit a bit overpriced for the content you receive (mainly looking at ariandel here)
-Cool bosses
-Combat is unbelievably smooth
-As usual, the games in the souls series have immense replayability
-Lots of armor/weapons to pick and play with
The bad:
-Enemies never seem to run out of stamina
-Weapon balance is terrible in PvP, there's a couple weapons which you will encounter every other fight
-Phantom hits in online play
-Shields are pretty much useless in PvE/PvP
-All areas are made out of either a brown or grey colour, which gets tiring rather quick
-Poise mechanic is executed poorly
-It barely matters whether you equip heavy or light armor.
-The newly introduced Weapon Arts, while cool, lead to an incredibly stale pvp-experience where you will encounter the same kind of repeated weapon art combo every time.
-Weapon arts are pretty much useless in most of the PvE content compared to regular attacks
Having said all this, I'd give Dark Souls 3 (Including DLC)  a solid 6/10
It's a worthwhile game to pick up if you're fresh to the souls series, but as a fan of the souls-series, I can't recommend it.

This is a purely performance based review.  Like so many people here, I have a very high end PC.  With max settings, I get over 70fps. I game in SUHD 4k resolution and the switch from high to ultra low FPS causes my monitor to resync itself.  Yes, it is my problem due to my chosen hardware... but what is not my problem is the arbitrary design decision to implement a low FPS mode for every other action in the game.  This causes me a neverending amount of frustration as my monitor constantly has to toggle between display modes.  I can see this happening with games made in 2005... but COME ON ALREADY!  30fps locks are for console gamers with limited memory... not for PC gamers with 64 bit operating systems and upwards of 16GB of memory.

I seem to edit this review every few years, and I feel as if every time this game has just gotten better and better. I will never forget the feeling that came over me when I first saw the trailer for this game, which was now over 4 years ago. I was somewhat younger, and the ideas and potential blew me away! Adventually I recieved this game as a gift, I can honeslty say it was the first game I really sat down and played for hours and hours. It took a while, but in some of the early beta stages the game began to feel tedious, and sooner or later I turned away from the game. Some while later, I began to hear about the upcoming full launch of the game, so for the weeks before I began to play again. Re-learning old things, aswell as figuring out some of what was new. As said prior this went on for a few weeks, all the way uo until 1.0 dropped... And when it did, oh my god did it deliver. What once turned me away from this game had vanished, there was suddenly a compelling story, interesting characters, meaning to the amazing bosses this game holds, and so, so much more! Beyond everything that this game has done thus far, the amazing devs at chucklefish continue to release amazing updates ever so often for the game! It would seem now that I am rambling on, and I have begun to notice several spelling errors in this reviw (my condolances). So, to bring this review to a close. Starbound is a truly incredible game, one that has never dissapointed me. It is a game where no matter how many times I return, no matter how many years it's been, it always finds some way to amaze me. Let it be known that this is most likely not my last review of the game, and there probably will be no "Last Review". Because starbound is a game that can't truly be described by words, it's something you have to play!

X-COM 2 is a decent game which builds upon the concepts of the first game. While the core elements have remained unchanged, Firaxis has introduced some new aspects to the game, of which the biggest disappointment to me is that most of the missions (and more importantly - the campaign) are time-limited.
Most missions have a timer in the upper-right corner which decreases with each turn you take. The campaign seems to be time-limited too. The aliens are building an 'avatar', a god knows what (I have not reached that point yet), and with each day you spend on side missions the avatar progress bar is filling.
This makes me feeling being artificially pushed towards the main quest, which I hate. So, if you, like me, prefer a more relaxed playthrough, I'd recommend skipping this title. Hopefully Firaxis will release a patch one day that will allow to disable or tweak these timers. I'd prefer something like the game speed option we could see in the Civilization series.
But if you don't mind the clocks ticking, you'll definitely enjoy the game.

Farwell my beloved Dark Souls. No other game will ever take your place in my heart. Thank you for all the times you killed me and made me rage. You taught me how to enjoy a hard game, how to power through difficulty, and how to git gud. The lessons you have taught me have made me better at games in general and more appreciative of difficulty and tribulation. Thank you.
Now for the review. I absolutely love the game and I highly recommend it. It has alot of problems and shortfalls when compared to it's masterpiece of a predecessor, but it is a far better game with more quality than most games on the market. Having four endings is wonderful in my opinion. Multiple ending games are always great. It simplified the upgrade system and requires no armor upgrades (which is awesome because now you can wear whatever you want without having to worry about upgrading the armor). It's DLC was good and worthwhile in my opinion though the second one was a complete let down... Still worth while. The Second DLC actually was very good and an excellent challenge for high level characters. It was otherwise alot like the first Dark Souls.
The only complaint I have is that the covenants are complete hogwash. Dark Souls 2 did a much better job as did Dark Souls 1 but DS2 did it better in my opinion. Instead of having NPC's and rivalries between covenant members you have alters that you bring items too and they will give you an item or two... Disappointing in this regard.
Overall I am happy and I am looking forward to what FromSoftware has in store for us in the future.

I've only played for few hours, but so far it feels like a winner. There's some performance issues, but they can't be too bad since my GTX 680 can run it on 2560x1440 resolution without trouble as long as I don't use Screen Space Reflections and if I want some extra FPS disabling antialiasing will add few more, but isn't strictly speaking necessary.
As a comparison, I can barely run Witcher 3 on that resolution on near-full settings and get 20-30fps. Admittedly, most other games I can run on full settings no problems.
Now, some people might have bigger problems, but thank god, I don't have them.
The only complaint is a minor one, and it's the loading times on going to mission, and back. It's not a huge long load, but considering the amount you'll be seeing the screen, it can add up.
More importantly, the tactical combat is still fully functional and with several changes it's improved on certain key aspects. The combat UI is still nonsensical in the details (the shortcut numbers for overwatch change depending on character and their available skills, which makes no sense), but that was same in the EU as well.
The only problem is the opressive timers, but assuming you can think tactically, it's not unconquerable obstacle. It does, however remove all camping style play that was the prevalent tactic in the EU and EW. So if you are in habit of taking those approaches, you will get busted and badly.
Now, the timers are a bit of an issue, but there's already few gazillion mods that either modify them, remove them, lengthen them, or any number of variants. So it's really a non-issue unless you're determined to be obstinate. I'm pretty confident that either Firaxis will fix any remaining issues (timers or other balance problems), or the modders will. So in the spirit of everyone who is a fan of Bethesda games, I am saying: IT'S PERFECT! MODDERS WILL FIX IT!
Seriously, though, it seems to be pretty spot on and I can't imagine what kind of mayhem modders will be able to create with a groundwork this solid.

2014 was the year where nothing got done for this game.

The christmas update although not officially stable it was more stable than their nightly and and previous unstable builds.
Later on in early 2015 they've released the update with a few refined things here and there and of course stability.
After playing the new update I can gladly say, that this game is pretty great.
Far more in-depth than in previous updates.

And the new biomes are pretty fantastic and the world maps are much more larger and it's full of goodies compared to the barren wastelands that were in the previous version of the game.
Overall this new update has brought along a satisfying experience.

Most reviews of Fallout 4 go one of two ways, either like this: "FALLOUT 4 IS THE BEST GAME EVER MADE BY PEOPLE!!!!!!! I SKIPPED MY GRANDMA'S FUNERAL TO PLAY IT LULZZZZZ", or else like this -- "Fallout 4 is garbage compared to the other Fallout games, go play New Vegas and don't touch this flaming turd". I have never played any other games in the series, so unburdened by expectations, I entered into it with a clean conscience. And I loved it. The world is unique and creative, and remarkably well-designed. The post-nuclear 50's-esque theme is retro and somehow eerily relevant to the present at the same time. The characters are varied and fun, the missions are many, and the vast crafting mechanic is executed well. However, as much as I love the mindless carnage of an FPS combined with the hoarding of items, I do have a few issues. First, the main story line of the vanilla game is far too short. No, no spoilers here, but I will say I was very disappointed with how quickly the game was "over". And that brings me to gripe number two: the add-on content is generally weak. A lot of the DLC is for crafting and building, which if you're really into that is great, but for those of us who want new story lines and missions, really the only ones worth getting are Automatron and Far Harbor (see those reviews for more details). TL;DR -- is it a great game? Yes. Does it offer excellent replayability? Meh, perhaps. Is it fun as hell? Yes. Sure, maybe the other games are more true to the RPG genre, but weighed on its own merits, Fallout 4 is more than worth the price of admission. (8/10)

I'm writing this review, in part, in response to the dozens of negative reviews I've seen for this game. While I can respect and understand the criticism this game has received over software bugs, divergence from the depth and feel of earlier Fallout games, etc., I feel many of the critics are responding out of anger because Fallout 4 is not Fallout: New Vegas II or Fallout 1 Rebooted. It's true, Fallout 4 is a much different game than its predecessors and is in many ways "watered down", even compared to Fallout 3 (which itself was excoriated in some quarters for not being a "real" Fallout game because it was first-person). The dialogue choices are not as deep or far reaching as in F3/FNV, The settlement building mechanic is both shallow and cumbersome. Some of the DLC has underwhelmed. But you know what? I've played more than 500 hours of F4, and I'm still having fun. I'm slowly working my way through all of the quests and DLCs, exploring modding options, and enjoying myself. By comparison, I have tried to start Fallout 3 and New Vegas several (actually, many several) times over the past decade or so (first on PC, later on XBox) and have given up every time. I simply didn't have the time or the patience to give the games what they needed. And as time passed, the games started to look uglier and uglier (and I thought F3 was ugly back in 2009). So as much as people crowed about the brilliance of the prior games, I just couldn't get into them. I write this not to bait anyone who adores the earlier games but to point out reasons why F4 is going to be worth some gamers' time. It is graphically much, much prettier than the earlier games, and if graphics are important to you, you will prefer it. Also, the art style is tweaked to be a bit more accessible to most gamers. The first-person shooting aspects are also better (VATS seems much the same, but in-the moment combat is improved). Also, if you have a modern computer running a recent version of Windows, it will run better than the earlier games (I've struggled for years to get/keep Fallout 3 running and stable on Win7/8/10. Also, even if the RPG elements are de-emphasized in this iteration, they are still there. It's not an RPG fan's wet dream, but it is a great RPG for people coming from an FPS background. If you're new to the Fallout universe and are looking for an accessible way in, Fallout 4 is a fantastic place to start. It's not a perfect game by any means,  but it is still a very good game that is worth a look  by anyone who loves story driven action games with RPG elements.

X-COM 2 is a decent game which builds upon the concepts of the first game. While the core elements have remained unchanged, Firaxis has introduced some new aspects to the game, of which the biggest disappointment to me is that most of the missions (and more importantly - the campaign) are time-limited.
Most missions have a timer in the upper-right corner which decreases with each turn you take. The campaign seems to be time-limited too. The aliens are building an 'avatar', a god knows what (I have not reached that point yet), and with each day you spend on side missions the avatar progress bar is filling.
This makes me feeling being artificially pushed towards the main quest, which I hate. So, if you, like me, prefer a more relaxed playthrough, I'd recommend skipping this title. Hopefully Firaxis will release a patch one day that will allow to disable or tweak these timers. I'd prefer something like the game speed option we could see in the Civilization series.
But if you don't mind the clocks ticking, you'll definitely enjoy the game.

Now, I'll be serious.
Darkest Dungeon is a turn-based 2D Rougelike RPG, made in Lovecraftian setting and greatly transfers atmoshpere of his books with Dungeons & Dragons rules into a game.
It is very dark, unforgiving and always, ALWAYS, requires you to listen, watch and think. What does it mean? As it is turn-based, it means, you have unlimited time to think about your next move and it's consequences. If you compare it to the other games, first one, to come up to your mind will be "Dark Souls". These games share hardcoreness and some sets of rules. Both of them require your attention and severly punish you for your carelessness. Overestimated yourself? Your hero dies or get serious injuries and won't be able to continue his journey. Hero's death here is permanent. You cannot resurrect them. At the beggining of the game it is, of course, tragedy, but at the end, when your heroes at levels 4-6, it becomes a catastrophic disaster to see as your trained, skilled, upgraded character dies from the claw of some big gargoyle.
Unlike any other games, this one introduces interesting mechanic - stress level. Here, your heroes are normal people, who can be scared by monsters in dungeons, and, as the matter of fact, they can mentally break. All this develops a mental connection with your character: you care about him, try to calculate risks. But sometimes, luck is just not on your side. And people will die. This game requires sacrifices, because it is the only way to teach you a lesson from your, at the first sight, tiny mistake.   For example, you see square-like dungeon with 9 rooms and the entering in the centre. You complete 8 rooms without any difficulty but the last room remains unexplored, and, of course, you want to explore it. You walk the hallway and see the altar. What could go wrong? As you touch the altar, your heroes teleport into some other dimensions with a huge and scary monster without any ability to escape. This thing wipes out all of your heroes, who were level 4, had very rare artifacts and upgraded skills. And all of this happens because monster CRITed you 2 times, your party gone mad and were unable to respond properly.
So, if you want hardcore experience, like D'n'D, Lovecraft, Rougelike games, this is your choice.

I've only played for few hours, but so far it feels like a winner. There's some performance issues, but they can't be too bad since my GTX 680 can run it on 2560x1440 resolution without trouble as long as I don't use Screen Space Reflections and if I want some extra FPS disabling antialiasing will add few more, but isn't strictly speaking necessary.
As a comparison, I can barely run Witcher 3 on that resolution on near-full settings and get 20-30fps. Admittedly, most other games I can run on full settings no problems.
Now, some people might have bigger problems, but thank god, I don't have them.
The only complaint is a minor one, and it's the loading times on going to mission, and back. It's not a huge long load, but considering the amount you'll be seeing the screen, it can add up.
More importantly, the tactical combat is still fully functional and with several changes it's improved on certain key aspects. The combat UI is still nonsensical in the details (the shortcut numbers for overwatch change depending on character and their available skills, which makes no sense), but that was same in the EU as well.
The only problem is the opressive timers, but assuming you can think tactically, it's not unconquerable obstacle. It does, however remove all camping style play that was the prevalent tactic in the EU and EW. So if you are in habit of taking those approaches, you will get busted and badly.
Now, the timers are a bit of an issue, but there's already few gazillion mods that either modify them, remove them, lengthen them, or any number of variants. So it's really a non-issue unless you're determined to be obstinate. I'm pretty confident that either Firaxis will fix any remaining issues (timers or other balance problems), or the modders will. So in the spirit of everyone who is a fan of Bethesda games, I am saying: IT'S PERFECT! MODDERS WILL FIX IT!
Seriously, though, it seems to be pretty spot on and I can't imagine what kind of mayhem modders will be able to create with a groundwork this solid.

After spending lots of time playing Spiral Knights, I simply can't recommend this game to other gamers, especially players new to the game.
Instead of working on and releasing new playable content into the SK world, the team at OOO pours their time into making useless accessories, costumes and variant skins, none of which impact the actual gameplay.  It's great for those who enjoy peacocking in a digital world among mostly tweens, but otherwise it's rather unfortunate.
In the years I've played it, the game has simply lacked in progression.  Then, sadly, when new holiday or special event "limited-time" levels are introduced, the developers focus on making the level as difficult and un-fun as possible. These short-lived levels force you to grind for new collectables in order to attain the object of your desire, all the while getting killed over and over again, forcing you to, essentially, pay-to-play (and/or waste lots of hours grinding... but time is money, no?).
I wish I had more positive things to say about SK... I really wish I could tell you that the story and levels keep getting better and better... that the gameplay is a ton of fun and that the majority of the people you meet won't beg you for your currency or items... that new bosses are being introduced and new strategies keep things interesting... that being in and/or owning a guild has any sort of point whatsoever... that the best update was better than 30-second speed boosts so you don't waste so much time running down long empty halls in each depth...
... but I can't... nope... not at this time at least... maybe in a few years... if it doesn't go the way of OOO's Dr. Who: World's in Time

If you're used to overwatch turtling or relying on snipers, you may find it difficult to adapt.  However, the intro missions do a good job of showing you how to play fast and aggressive. A few performance issues with high details (would hardly be noticable if I wasn't so familiar with the first game) and an annoying sort of 'interference' feature on all dialog windows in the game.  However, the rest is solid.

Reviewing this game is tough. If you have never played a fallout game before, this is a great game to kill some time and set aside after completing it. However, if you are someone who has played fallout 1, 2, 3, and new vegas, I don't know if I could recommend this game to you. Fallout 4 does not play like an RPG where you get to create your own backstory and choose how to approach any situation, Fallout 4 is an on-the-rails shooter disguised as an RPG. The clever dialogue system native to Bethesda games is totally gone in this iteration of Fallout, replaced by a half-baked Bioware-style dialogue interface with 4 "choices" of dialogue. A glaring flaw in this system is the way you approach dialogue has a minimal impact on the way the story plays out. What is a Bethesda game without freedom? In fact, (minor spoiler alert), the ending of the game has you choose between 3 functionally identical outcomes. Compare this to New Vegas, where you had countless choices of how the game ended, from the extent of House's control over New Vegas to the NCR/Legion's influence in the Mojave. While you could leave the mojave unchanged by leaving House, the NCR, and the Legion in power, you could also liberate the Mojave by forcing these powers out, whether through violent or peaceful means. Additionally, New Vegas's DLC expands on the main story in a fascinating way, adding even more replay value to the game. Now, back to Fallout 4, Far Harbor is a very good DLC. Far Harbor brings the character back to the roots of the Fallout series, offering a pretty significant amount of choice while also tying in to the main story. In fact, if you can get fallout 4 and far harbor for 50% off, I think it is worth playing through the main story and Far Harbor in order to experience the well-written story and interesting side quests (which beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of the base game's side quests). Overall, I did enjoy playing Fallout 4, but I was very disappointed by how Bethesda drastically changed (dare I say dumbed down) one of my favorite series of games, to the detriment of long-term Fallout fans and even those who expected an RPG.

Pros:
1. It's the same gameplay as XCOM: Enemy Unknown / Enemy Within:
a. The same camera as before.
b. The same placement cursor as before.
2. It's unforgiving, as it's supposed to be.
3. New enemies means new tactics. Forget the tactics you used before.
4. More customisation options for your soldiers.
Cons:
1. It's the same gameplay as XCOM: Enemy Unknown / Enemy Within
a. The same camera as before; which will hide important events when it decides to focus on the floor above you instead of hiding that to show you what's going on on the floor you're actually on. NEEDS AUTOROTATION AND PROPER ELEMENT HIDING!
b. The same placement cursor as before; Which will occasionally jump floors or move to a position right next to where you think you have your cursor, moving soldiers out of cover, into view of the enemy, into fire...
2. The graphics are badly optimized both on Windows and Linux, on both NVIDIA and AMD videocards.
3. It's a severe memory hog.
a. It will lock down even faster systems while loading itself into memory or unloading itself when exiting to desktop.
b. Mission areas don't load properly all the time.
4. It further removed base building from the original XCOM setup, which is the wrong direction to go in. I'm all for having a mobile base, but it's even more cramped and useless than the underground base from XCOM: Enemy Unknown / Enemy Within. Bring back the option to set up multiple bases in XCOM 3, if it ever comes to that... And what's with needing to assign engineers to "excavate" within a vehicle? It makes little sense to me.
5. The new customisation options layout for your troops is confusing to work with
a. I find myself having to skip back and forth through the different layers of menus to find the right options. The location of the items are not intuitively placed.
b. And still no option to save an outfit design so you can easily copypaste them to other troops.
6. The introductionary mission effectively leaves you with two dead soldiers in your memorial... sad times all around.
7. Too many round timers!
Overall I recommend this game for those who played XCOM: Enemy Within and enjoyed rushing missions to get meld. The barrage of round timers mostly reminded me of that, and can get annoying at times.
But I would also recommend waiting until there's been a few patches to optimize the game. Right now it runs slow as hell, the video and audio can move out of sync, and there's still the horrid camera which hides shots taken. This needs to be fixed.
